💡 Key Takeaways
  • EXCLUSIVE: Louis Garrel and Harry Lawtey are set to join Jeremy Allen White in the Laika Live Action and A24 World War II survival thriller Airman directed by Ben Stiller.
  • Based on the Latest York Times bestseller The Lost Airman: A True Story of Escape from Nazi-Occupied France by Seth Meyerowitz, the film recounts the harrowing and remarkable untold story of Arthur Meyerowitz, who was shot down over Nazi-occupied France and evaded Gestapo pursuers for months before attempting a daring escape.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EXCLUSIVE: Louis Garrel and Harry Lawtey are set to join Jeremy Allen White in the Laika Live Action and A24 World War II survival thriller Airman directed by Ben Stiller.

Based on the Latest York Times bestseller The Lost Airman: A True Story of Escape from Nazi-Occupied France by Seth Meyerowitz, the film recounts the harrowing and remarkable untold story of Arthur Meyerowitz, who was shot down over Nazi-occupied France and evaded Gestapo pursuers for months before attempting a daring escape. The book was published in 2016 by Penguin.

Sources indicate that the script is by Ben Shattuck and Stiller. Three-time Oscar winner Emmanuel Lubezki has been tapped as director of photography, Christian Goldbeck as production designer, Małgorzata Karpiuk as costume designer and Geoffrey Richman as editor.

Industry observers note that laika Live Action will lead production alongside A24, which will also handle domestic distribution and international sales. The film is a Le Grisbi Productions and Storyteller Productions production, in association with Red Hour Films and Nine Stories. Watch on Deadline.

It has been revealed that stiller will produce for his Red Hour Films as will John Lesher for his Le Grisbi Productions, PJ van Sandwijk for his Storyteller Productions, Travis Knight and Matt Levin for Laika, and A24. Executive producers are Maryse Knight, Jeremy Kipp Walker and Zac Locke for Laika, Michael Lesslie and Marie Savare for Storyteller, Jake Gyllenhaal for Nine Stories and Miki Emmerich, Richard Whelan, Meyerowitz, Dan Bodansky and James Dixon. Gian Pablo Antonetti serves as co-producer for Le Grisbi.

It has been revealed that “We’re thrilled to partner with A24, Ben and Jeremy on a film that embodies our commitment to bold, filmmaker-driven cinema,” mentioned Matt Levin, Laika’s President of Live Action Film & Series. “Ben is an extraordinary talent with a singular creative vision, and we couldn’t be more excited to bring this incredible true story to life together.”.

Stiller is represented by WME, VIE and Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern. White is represented by WME. Garrel is represented by UTA and Agence Adequat. Lawtey is represented by CAA, B-Side and Goodman, Genow, Schenkman, Smelkinson & Christopher.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Yesterday Apple released its first post-launch software update for HomeView, less than a week after the product debuted.
  • Per the company’s official release notes, HomeView 27.2.1 focuses on bug fixes, including a fix for the following problem:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple’s new HomeView just launched last Friday, but some early adopters reported issues with Siri AI in their first days of use. Apple shipped fixes in HomeView 27.2.1 yesterday, but it also confirmed the iOS 27.3 beta is responsible for some of the problems.

Yesterday Apple released its first post-launch software update for HomeView, less than a week after the product debuted.

Per the company’s official release notes, HomeView 27.2.1 focuses on bug fixes, including a fix for the following problem:.

Pairing with an iPhone or iPad running the iOS or iPadOS 27.3 beta may cause Siri requests to fail.

It’s unknown how many reports of Siri problems on HomeView can be attributed to the iOS 27.3 beta. However, it wouldn’t surprise me if many of the reports were from beta customers. That’s in part because early HomeView reviewers didn’t seem to have the same problems.

With HomeView 27.2.1 now available, those problems should hopefully be taken care of. However, if you’re on the iOS 27.3 beta, there’s a new issue you’ll need to deal with temporarily.

As discovered by pdfu, if you try to make a Personal Content request on an iPhone running iOS 27.3, Siri in HomeView 27.2.1 now states: “I can’t help with that because your personal device is on newer software.”.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re on iOS 27.3, Siri on HomeView can’t use your iPhone for personal context, likely until December.HomeView won’t send Siri requests to an iPhone on newer software. Without a HomeView patch, your only option is iOS 27.2.x.On-device requests like timers still work. https://t.co/8UbRs7z496.

Industry observers note that it’s understandable that issues might arise from having iOS and HomeView software that’s out of sync. Unfortunately though, there’s no beta software available for HomeView at the moment.

That means unless Apple releases a beta soon, users might have to wait until the public launch of HomeView 27.3 in December to get Personal Content features back.

How has Siri AI been working for you on HomeView? Let us know in the comments.

GTA 6’s 30 FPS lock broke my PC gamer brain — until I turned on the one TV setting I swore I’d never touch

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (947 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you’ve ever bought a new TV and invited a tech nerd like me into your living room, you already know I’m grabbing your remote, diving into the picture settings, and disabling motion smoothing.
  • For movies and prestige TV, it is a crime against humanity — turning a cinematic masterpiece into an episode of "Days of Our Lives" shot on a camcorder.
  • And yet, here I am, playing Grand Theft Auto VI with motion smoothing cranked on, and refusing to turn it off.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’ve ever bought a new TV and invited a tech nerd like me into your living room, you already know I’m grabbing your remote, diving into the picture settings, and disabling motion smoothing.

For movies and prestige TV, it is a crime against humanity — turning a cinematic masterpiece into an episode of "Days of Our Lives" shot on a camcorder. I hate it. Tom Cruise hates it. You should hate it too.

And yet, here I am, playing Grand Theft Auto VI with motion smoothing cranked on, and refusing to turn it off.

Industry observers note that to understand how I ended up committing TV heresy, you have to understand the shock to the system that is GTA 6’s frame rate. Coming straight from my monster PC rig playing games like Resident Evil Requiem at up to 214 FPS, dropping back down to a strict 30 FPS console lock feels like wading through treacle.

But on top of that, as I’ve seen (and you’ve seen on Digital Foundry’s test), that 30 FPS lock isn’t an actual lock. It can dip into the mid-20s during heavy scenes. Coming from super fluidity, that 30 FPS is brutal to adapt to.

So out of sheer desperation (and because we’re stuck waiting for the PC port), I broke the golden rule and toggled my TV’s smooth motion setting on.

And I hate to admit it, but it’s basically bootleg DLSS Frame Generation for your living room.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Just like PC frame generation tricks of old, your TV’s motion interpolation processor looks at two real frames from your console, guesses what should happen in between them, and inserts an artificial frame to smooth out the motion.

In a recent development, the moment I flipped it on in GTA 6, that nauseating camera stutter when cruising down Ocean Beach vanished. Panning around a crowded street or taking a high-speed corner suddenly felt dramatically more fluid — nowhere near 60 fps, and definitely not my desktop rig, but miles smoother than the choppy presentation.

Sources indicate that before the AV forums come for my head with pitchforks, let’s be completely honest about the trade-offs. There is no such thing as a free lunch in frame interpolation:.

According to recent reports, because your TV has to wait for the next frame before it can invent the one in the middle, motion smooth adds latency between pressing a button and seeing the result on screen. In twitchy, competitive games, that’s a death sentence.

But in a Rockstar open-world game — where character movement is already famously weighty and deliberate — I never noticed that extra latency.

Your TV’s processor is just guessing after all, and while it is a good guesser, there are some moments of weird shimmering around fast-moving objects and some boiling around on-screen elements like subtitles. Probably compounded by the fact GTA 6 is already running its own resolution scaling tech under the hood.

Standard Game Mode and VRR (Variable Refresh Rate) automatically lock out motion smoothing on many TVs. Depending on your set, you either have to turn on the dedicated low-latency Game Motion Plus mode (found on newer Samsung and LG sets) or sacrifice VRR to unlock it.

The silver lining, though, is that with this being a 30 FPS game, it’s not high enough to require VRR anyway.

If GTA 6’s 30 FPS cap is giving your eyes a workout and you want to test the dark arts yourself, don’t just blindly max out every slider.

If your TV has a low-latency interpolation option (like Samsung’s Game Motion Plus or LG’s TruMotion tweaks), use that before turning off Game Mode completely.

Set Judder Reduction to a middle ground (around 5-7 out of 10) rather than maxing it out. You want to take the harsh edge off camera pans without turning your car into a blurry smudge.

It has been revealed that this is optional based on personal taste. Test how your TV’s smoothing looks with GTA’s built-in motion blur turned off. For a lot of OLED owners, letting the TV handle the smoothing cleanly beats stacking two different blur effects on top of each other.

Industry observers note that do I want to play GTA 6 at native 240 FPS on my PC rig? Obviously. The second Rockstar drops the PC version, I’ll be uninstalling this hack from my brain and never looking back.

Recent findings suggest that I still wouldn’t be caught dead watching a movie with motion smoothing turned on. But until PC gamers get their turn in Vice City, breaking the ultimate TV rule is the best survival trick I’ve found for making a 30 FPS masterpiece actually feel better to play.

In a recent development, also yes, my wife has taken note of the fact that I share the same name as the male protagonist. And yes, she is side-eyeing how I treat Lucia hard.

Industry News: Microsoft To Do is retiring, including Mac and iOS apps

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Microsoft is saying goodbye to its task management service To Do, including the Mac and iOS apps.
  • Recent findings suggest that the last day to use the To Do apps is June 30, 2027.
  • Sources indicate that “Microsoft To Do is retiring,” Microsoft explains.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Microsoft is saying goodbye to its task management service To Do, including the Mac and iOS apps. Here’s what people need to know.

Recent findings suggest that the last day to use the To Do apps is June 30, 2027. That date also applies to Windows, Android, and the web. The underlying service and sync support will retire later, according to Microsoft’s support document.

Sources indicate that “Microsoft To Do is retiring,” Microsoft explains. “For work or school accounts, Microsoft Planner will be the destination for managing personal work tasks alongside assigned work. The updated My tasks experience begins rolling out in December 2026.”.

Recent findings suggest that on the Mac, you can use Planner on the web or in Teams. Microsoft explicitly claims it has no looks for a native Mac app.

You can still see your existing To Do tasks in Planner through June 30, but your tasks and lists won’t carry over. Microsoft aims to offer an export option before the apps retire.

Planner doesn’t support personal Microsoft accounts however. If that’s how you use To Do, you’ll need to pick another task manager, even if you pay for Microsoft 365 Personal or Family, according to the company.

It has been revealed that the June shutdown will end a run of just over a decade for To Do on Apple platforms. Microsoft bought the firm behind Wunderlist in 2015 and released the first iPhone preview of To Do in April 2017.

Looking for a proper replacement? Apple’s built-in Reminders app can keep lists in sync between Apple devices, including a grocery list you share with family through iCloud.

Microsoft has been trying to make Teams as the super app for some time now, as Planner is integrated into Teams. Teams is one of the prime examples of why super apps are terrible, with a bloated, web app-like experience.

If you liked To Do because it worked across platforms, Todoist has apps for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Windows, and Android.

According to recent reports, does this sunsetting affect you? Were you a Wunderlist user back in the day? Share your thoughts in the comments.

Revision: Howard Crow, Director of Product, Agents and AI, Microsoft, shared this statement with 9to5Mac regarding the transition:.

According to recent reports, “We’re bringing task management experiences together across Microsoft 365 to make it easier for customers to manage individual tasks and team plans. As part of this transition, Microsoft To Do apps will retire on June 30, 2027, with work and school experiences coming together in Microsoft Planner. Existing integrations across Microsoft 365, including Outlook and Teams, will also be updated to work with Planner. We recognize this change will affect customers differently, particularly those using personal Microsoft accounts, and we’re committed to helping them prepare. Customers will be able to export their To Do data before retirement, and we’ll share additional guidance to support the transition.”.

Elin Hilderbrand’s ’28 Summers’ & ‘The Rumor’ Series Adaptations In Works At 20th Television With ‘Five Star Weekend’ EPs & ‘Perfect Couple’ Creator

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (768 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Deadline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that EXCLUSIVE: Elin Hilderbrand‘s Nantucket TV universe is expanding to a newly introduced studio.
  • Industry observers note that jenna Lamia, creator of another hit series based on a Hilderbrand novel set in Nantucket, Netflix’s The Perfect Couple, is set to write and executive produce The Rumor.
  • Industry observers note that lamia has another series adaptation of a Hilderbrand bestseller, Winter Street, in the works at Disney.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that EXCLUSIVE: Elin Hilderbrand‘s Nantucket TV universe is expanding to a newly introduced studio. 20th Television has optioned two popular novels by the bestselling author, 28 Summers and The Rumor, for Sue Naegle and Ali Krug‘s studio-based Dinner Party, which is behind Peacock’s popular adaptation of Hilderbrand’s The Five Star Weekend starring Jennifer Garner.

Industry observers note that jenna Lamia, creator of another hit series based on a Hilderbrand novel set in Nantucket, Netflix’s The Perfect Couple, is set to write and executive produce The Rumor. The 28 Summers and The Rumor series, both in early development, are executive produced by Hilderbrand, Naegle and Krug. They fall under the overall deal Naegle and Krug signed with 20th Television in September, moving their Dinner Party company to Disney from NBCUniversal. Related Stories Casting Karla Souza To Star In 'Grey's Anatomy' Texas Spinoff News ABC Developing Police Procedural From 'Government Cheese' Co-Creator Aeysha Carr and Ramón Rodríguez.

Industry observers note that lamia has another series adaptation of a Hilderbrand bestseller, Winter Street, in the works at Disney. The project, from indie studio wiip, is in development at Hulu. Watch on Deadline.

Inspired by 1978 film Same Time Next Year, 28 Summers explores the agony and romance of a one-weekend-per-year affair and the dramatic ways this relationship complicates and enriches their lives, and the lives of the people they love.

The novel, originally published in 2020, was previously optioned for development as a movie by MRC.

Written by Lamia based on Hilderbrand’s 2015 novel, The Rumor unfolds over a Nantucket summer in which island gossip turns dangerous, and the only person with the story straight is a local novelist who must decide whether to publish it.

The Bold Type co-executive producer Holly Whidden, a Nantucket insider who was a consulting producer on The Perfect Couple, also serves as executive producer.

According to recent reports, “I’m thrilled to have two of my most beloved novels adapted by Dinner Party, the production team who turned The Five Star Weekend into an elevated, spellbinding, and hugely successful series,” Hilderbrand stated. “I’m grateful to Karey Burke at 20th TV for championing my work and assembling such a quality team, including Jenna Lamia, who created The Perfect Couple. I could not be more optimistic about the future of the ‘Hilder-verse’ in Hollywood.”.

Sources indicate that some of the optimism likely stems from the performance of Netflix’s The Perfect Couple and Peacock’s The Five Star Weekend. Both were developed and produced as limited series, and both became franchises after the initial installment’s ratings success.

The Five Star Weekend, created by Bekah Brunstetter, has been renewed for a second season featuring the same core characters, with Naegle and Krug executive producing.

The Perfect Couple is taking an anthology approach with a potential second season, now in development, based on another Hilderbrand novel, Swan Song.

Naegle also executive produces Peacock’s thriller drama The Day of the Jackal, which is returning for a second season. It is produced by Universal Global Television, the studio behind The Perfect Couple.

Industry observers note that prior to launching Dinner Party Prods., Naegle served as Chief Content Officer at Annapurna Pictures, overseeing TV, Film, and Theatre, with Krug as her Co-Head of Television. The two executive produced Hulu’s Pam & Tommy and Monsterland as well as HBO Max’s The Staircase, starring Colin Firth and Toni Collette; Prime Video’s Dead Ringers, starring Rachel Weisz; Apple TV’s The Changeling, starring LaKeith Stanfield; and Netflix’s Soundtrack. Naegle began her career at UTA, rising to partner and co-head of the TV Lit Department before being appointed President of HBO Entertainment in 2008. She and Krug are repped by UTA.

Industry observers note that in addition to serving as creator, executive producer and showrunner on The Perfect Couple, starring Nicole Kidman and Liev Schreiber, Lamia co-executive produced NBC’s Good Girls and co-executive produced MTV’s Awkward, appearing in seasons 4 and 5. She also was a writer and recurring cast member on Syfy’s Resident Alien. In film, Lamia wrote and produced the supernatural comedy horror My Best Friend’s Exorcism for Amazon based on the novel by Grady Hendrix. She is repped by UTA and Ben Rubinfeld at Ziffren.

Hilderbrand is repped by UTA, InkWell Management and Kleinberg, Lange, Cuddy & Carlo. Whidden, who also was a consulting producer on HBO’s The Undoing, is repped by Karen Gottlieb at Grubman Shire Meiselas & Sacks.

According to recent reports, baking visual intelligence into Camera should expose the feature to a lot more iPad consumers, since before you had to set up a custom control or shortcut for it. It has been revealed that but the hardware alone doesn’t define the experience—Nothing’s control scheme is what makes these wireless headphones stand out. Instead of touch panels or clunky buttons, you get a satisfying volume scroll wheel (they call it the Roller), a multi-function Paddle for track navigation, and a customizable button that can switch EQ profiles or noise modes. You also get spatial audio and multipoint Bluetooth support, which work well across Android and iOS.

Sources indicate that that said, the earcups aren’t the softest for long sessions, and while they’re padded, the shape might not suit everyone. Performance-wise, the ANC handles low-end noise well (think airplane engines and AC hum) but struggles with sharper, unexpected sounds like clanging dishes or chatter nearby. As for its sound profile, it leans towards the punchier side, especially with a bit of EQ tweaking in the app, but you’ll need to put in some effort if you want the best results, notes this PCMag review.

Amazon has reduced the price of all its own-brand soundbars, including the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar for just $74, the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus for $139, the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar with Subwoofer for $229, and the Amazon Fire TV Soundbar with Subwoofer and Rears for $349.

Candle Media’s Kevin Mayer Indicates Company Caught Out By Drop In Streamer Demand: “We Didn’t See That Contraction Coming”

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Candle Media cofounder Kevin Mayer told an industry conference in Doha on Friday that he had not foreseen the impending contraction in demand for streaming content in 2023, ahead of the company’s launch in 2021.
  • He was speaking six weeks after Candle Media hit the trade headlines for its sale of Reece Witherspoon’s Hello Sunshine to Paris-based European content group Mediawan.
  • Candle Media originally acquired the manufacturer, behind Big Little Lies and The Morning Show, in 2021, as one of its first acquisitions for $900M.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Candle Media cofounder Kevin Mayer told an industry conference in Doha on Friday that he had not foreseen the impending contraction in demand for streaming content in 2023, ahead of the company’s launch in 2021.

He was speaking six weeks after Candle Media hit the trade headlines for its sale of Reece Witherspoon’s Hello Sunshine to Paris-based European content group Mediawan.

Candle Media originally acquired the manufacturer, behind Big Little Lies and The Morning Show, in 2021, as one of its first acquisitions for $900M. The re-sale price was not made public, but sources told Deadline that it was likely several hundreds of millions of dollars less than the original price. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Doha Film Festival Lifts Off As Gulf States Remain On High Alert Amid Iran Attacks Books Elle And Dakota Fanning Rebel In First Trailer For 'The Nightingale' Based On Kristin Hannah Best-Seller.

Mayer, who was talking to the Qatar Film Committee’s Industry Days event in Doha via video-link from L.A., did not dwell on the sale.

Sources indicate that “On the live action side, we gave it a really good shot with Hella Sunshine and other assets. It was okay, but they didn’t work out to what we wanted, so we recently sold those,” he stated.

Mayer did not go into details on why Hello Shine had not worked out for Candle Media, and there were no opportunities for questions from the floor.

His wider discussion, however, gave insight into some of the challenges facing the tech giant as well as its triumphs led by its acquisition of Moonbug Entertainment, the children’s media company behind reveals such as CoComelon, Blippi and Little Angel.

The former Disney exec, who oversaw the studio’s 2019 acquisition of 20th Century Fox and also helped spearhead the creation of Disney+ alongside Bon Iger, said the idea for Candle Media had been sparked by the studios getting into streaming and taking their IP in-house.

This trend, he said, suggested that streamers without massive inhouse production capacity would be on the hunt for high-quality content.

According to recent reports, “We felt that the value of being independent in that sort of industry, that vertically integrated, would be increasing, and I think that is still true. Being independent and having that that ability to sell to any of the streaming services is great,” he remarked.

“We also thought content demand would continue to increase double digits a year… with increasing demand globally for high-quality content, like we were producing at Candle Media, which would provide us with the volume we needed to make all of our acquisitions work financially,” he continued.

Sources indicate that “Starting in 2023, that didn’t happen. In fact, the demand for streaming content actually contracted quite a bit, to about 35% below the peak of 2022. So, that part of our thesis was incorrect, unfortunately. We didn’t see that contraction coming.”.

The second premise on which the firm was built, he mentioned, was the belief that strong IP and stories could exist on multiple formats.

“They could exist on YouTube and on TikTok and on other platforms as short form entertainment… they could coexist in traditional film, on streaming and television and elsewhere,” he remarked. “Then they would open up other revenue platforms such as consumer products licensing, which we did a lot with Disney, games, music…”.

Mayer pointed to children’s media manufacturer Moonbug, which Candle Media acquired in 2021, as having fulfilled that goal thanks to demonstrates like CoCocomelon, which was born on YouTube, and then repackaged for Netflix.

Industry observers note that “We took those stories that came from YouTube, put them into one-hour compilations and licensed them to Netflix from 2021 to 2024. While CoComelon was the largest YouTube channel in the world, it was also the most popular Netflix show in the world. For three solid years, it was the number one streaming show and the number one YouTube show,” he said.

He mentioned the operation had not worked in the opposite direction for more traditional IP.

Recent findings suggest that “We were hopeful that we could take traditional film and TV and cross it over into social media. That didn’t work all that well. But what did work really well is taking social media storytelling and crossing it over to traditional. And you’ve seen Obsession and Backrooms… all this stuff is happening from that perspective.”.

Sources indicate that you can also move the latest slider incrementally to achieve exactly your ideal balance of Transparency and Noise Cancellation. It’s not limited to just a few preset options.

#16435. This Note-Taking Pebble Ring Is so Simple, and I Love It

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (903 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

This Note-Taking Pebble Ring Is so Simple, and I Love It

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (903 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, pebble’s $75 ring, the Index 01, has one job: It lets you record voice memos.
  • In a recent development, in this era where every tech product is trying to also be every other tech product, I appreciate the Index’s simplicity.
  • To buy the Index 01 ring, you get yourself a sizing kit (either buy one for $10 or 3D print it yourself), order the ring, and pair it with the Pebble app on your phone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, pebble’s $75 ring, the Index 01, has one job: It lets you record voice memos. That seems like it would be underwhelming, and the idea was ridiculed by some of Pebble’s fans when the product was first declared. But I’ve been wearing it for a few weeks, and folks: I love it.

In a recent development, in this era where every tech product is trying to also be every other tech product, I appreciate the Index’s simplicity. This is a ring with no heart rate sensors or even charging pins, just a microphone, a button to activate it, and a light to let you know that it’s working. The audio is processed on your device; no need to send anything to the cloud.

To buy the Index 01 ring, you get yourself a sizing kit (either buy one for $10 or 3D print it yourself), order the ring, and pair it with the Pebble app on your phone. I use an iPhone rather than an Android, which means I can’t use certain features like setting timed reminders or connecting to Beeper, but it’s still an incredibly useful little device. The Index has no charger, since it uses a disposable battery that Pebble estimates will last about two years.

Recent findings suggest that the simplest way to use the Index is to wear it on your index finger (hence the name, get it?) and press the button with your thumb. Speak a quick note while holding the button in, and the ring will flash to let you know it got the message. A moment later, you’ll get a notification saying that it added (whatever you said) to your “Notes to self” note.

Recent findings suggest that to take this further, you can create different notes and ask the ring to add what you say to a specific note. You can also double-click the button to ask a question. The answer will appear in the notification you get on your phone or watch a moment later. (The ring does not speak to you.).

According to recent reports, all the notes you leave yourself appear as plain text in the Pebble app, fully editable. If you tap on each one, you can see a timestamp from when you left the note, and you can replay the voice recording if the transcription doesn’t make sense. (Why is there a “pencil sharp pepper” on my packing list? Ohh, that’s a pencil sharpener.) You can also add notes by typing them, which I find useful when starting a to-do list or a packing list.

It’s incredible how useful a simple timestamped note can be. I used to do something similar with my “notes to self” chat in Signal, but the Index makes it even easier since I won’t get distracted by opening my phone. For example, I make a note on the Index whenever I take a medication, so that tomorrow morning I will be able to check whether I already took, say, a long-acting allergy pill. (You do not want to accidentally double up on those.).

Industry observers note that there’s one thing that, for years, I wished for a simple tool to help me do. It’s trivial, which makes it extra frustrating that I have not been able to find a good solution. I would simply like to note when I leave for a road trip, and when I start and end each stop. This way I can tell how long the driving took as a portion of the whole trip, and how long my stops tend to be so I can blueprint them better next time.

Recent findings suggest that you’d think this would be easy, but every existing tool drove me nuts in a different way. Stopwatches only store a single number, so I can’t break down how long each stop was—and if I miss a button press, I’m screwed. Sending myself a Signal text is probably my best option, but if I’ve just parked my car after three hours of driving, the second I pick up my phone I’m going to see all the notifications that arrived while I was on the road, and I’ll forget to actually send that text.

In a recent development, but this is exactly what the Index does well. I don’t even need to open my phone or look at my watch. Pressing the button with my thumb means I can do this one-handed without having a microphone always listening. (It’s also a great way to jot down the random things I think of while driving.).

The Index worked perfectly for my travel log, and I even used it for a workout after I got to my hotel room that night. I’d do 10 pushups, then tell the ring “add 10 pushups to my workout.” I’d do 20 crunches, and add that as well. I left the workout note open on my phone and could glance over and see what I had already done, since my messages got added to the note as I went.

It has been revealed that I didn’t need a workout app for any of this, or a special-purpose travel app. I can just leave myself a dang note, and the note-taking app can remember when I left the note and, if I choose, play back exactly how I noted it. It’s gloriously simple. Good job, Pebble.

Computer use lets Gemini for Mac click and type on your behalf to accomplish multi-step tasks in local desktop apps and the web, like navigating menus and filling out forms.

Google will pause for logins and payments, with confirmation needed for sensitive actions.

Many everyday tasks span desktop apps and websites that don’t connect to each other. Computer use handles the tedious steps in the background so you can save time without giving up your screen or cursor.

Industry representatives from trade groups and unions (below) spent the past week lobbying on Capitol Hill, but it’s unclear whether the legislation can pass during the lame duck session, which has been a goal of advocates, who warn of the production flight to other countries.

While there has been hope that the legislation could be attached to a year-end funding bill or a tax package, there are still doubts as to whether that will happen and what Republicans will prioritize in their final weeks in leadership. The press conference — which lasted for about 90 minutes — was heavy in Trump trumpeting his recent trip to Asia, which included a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. But it also turned out to be a tryout of sorts for his potential successor, as Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio stood by his side, occasionally swaying back and forth as Trump went on. They each made brief remarks.

Trump’s comment on the incentives legislation came in response to a question of how he will work with Congress’ Democratic leadership.

It has been revealed that “There are those that say we might get more done because we had some Republicans that were impossible to deal with,” Trump mentioned, citing Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY), who was defeated by a Trump-endorsed candidate in the primary.

It has been revealed that during the press conference, Trump scolded one reporter as she continued to shout a question about immigration, but he otherwise got into no major tiff with those gathered. “Thank you for your fairness and thank you for your questions,” Trump said as he ended the session.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, gemini Notebook, Google's AI tool for study and research, already lets you do a lot with your notes: You can turn them into flashcard quizzes, interactive podcasts, video explainers, mind maps, and infographics, as well as interrogating the sources you've collected through AI-powered prompts and responses.
  • Sources indicate that that might not immediately seem like the most obvious fit, turning your research notes into a mass of HTML code.
  • Recent findings suggest that website building is rolling out now for Gemini Notebook's web app for all users, and is "coming soon" to the mobile app.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, gemini Notebook, Google's AI tool for study and research, already lets you do a lot with your notes: You can turn them into flashcard quizzes, interactive podcasts, video explainers, mind maps, and infographics, as well as interrogating the sources you've collected through AI-powered prompts and responses. Now there's something new. You can also build interactive websites from your notebooks.

Sources indicate that that might not immediately seem like the most obvious fit, turning your research notes into a mass of HTML code. But it gives you another way to look at your material and to get insights from it. Here's how it works, what you could potentially do with it, and how impressively it worked when I put it to the test on some early 20th-century Irish literature.

Recent findings suggest that website building is rolling out now for Gemini Notebook's web app for all users, and is "coming soon" to the mobile app. You won't see a website option in the Studio panel alongside Audio Overview, Reports, Quiz, and the rest; instead, you type something along the lines of "make me a website" in the prompt box.

To make a website, you need sources, so I set Gemini Notebook to collect information about James Joyce's 1914 collection of short stories, Dubliners. As I studied Dubliners many years ago (I highly recommend it), I was hoping I'd spot any AI errors and hallucinations, and be able to properly assess the quality of Gemini Notebook's analysis.

With a suitable amount of information absorbed into the AI brain, I got Gemini Notebook to make me a website. Google doesn't give too much official guidance here, but says you should add "a description of what you want to build for work or study," so if you have a particular style or angle in mind, include it.

Here was my prompt: "Build a website using all the sources and information collected so far. Make it an interactive guide to the individual stories in Dubliners, as well as the overarching themes and context. I want to use it as a study aid to explore different aspects of the story collection.".

The finished website pops up in the Studio panel, and in my case it took around five minutes to put something together from 26 different sources. Click on the website, and it opens in a new window—you can use it from there, open it in a separate tab, or download the code to your computer.

I was honestly impressed by how much Gemini Notebook managed to pack into a single website: I got plot summaries, analysis, critical context, and some of the main themes and motifs outlined. There was an interactive quiz at the bottom of the page to test my knowledge, and even a graphic I could click through to reveal different elements of how the stories fit together.

In a recent development, everything was well laid out and functional, albeit with the standard "sheen" you get from anything made by AI (which tends to always pick the same colors and fonts). I wouldn't have necessarily thought that I needed a website if I was still studying Dubliners today, but I can definitely see how it would have helped.

According to recent reports, for something like my project, a website really works well as a study aid, since it offers a different way of interrogating the information. You can already do that in the main chat, and with tools such as the audio and video overviews, but this is different. It's a bit like having a mini-Wikipedia focused just on whatever you're researching.

The interactive elements that are included—so in my example, I could click from story to story, and theme to theme, within the same page—make a site more engaging than a standard report document and a static wall of text, and should help the information stick if you're trying to study it.

According to recent reports, I can also see how this might be useful for sharing data with others. Maybe you need to analyze monthly report figures, or you want to chart how your organization has developed a product over time—perhaps an interactive website will relay that information in a more compelling way than a slide deck or PDF.

Maybe you have a notebook stuffed with details of a significant family vacation. Putting together a website through Gemini Notebook would give your family a hub that they could use to easily check up on the details of the trip—where you're going and when, what you'll see there, what they need to pack, and so on. Another idea might be a family tree, if you have ancestry data and sources packed together in a notebook. Putting together a website would be a great way to visualize it, and, again, it's something you could share with relatives. If there were updates to the data you've collected, you could generate a new website.

Industry observers note that bear in mind that you can do a lot with your prompt. My website turned out the way it did because that's what I asked for, and if you need more interactivity or specific types of sections, then you can ask. Based on my follow-up prompts, you can also specify colors and certain layout choices, though it's not quite a full-scale website builder.

It looks like these sites are single-page creations, though they do have interactive elements and sections that change as you click around. It might be better to think of them as mini apps rather than sites. As of yet, there's no built-in option for publishing a site online or sharing it with others, so you need to download the HTML and do that manually.

Stream Yellowjackets on Paramount+.

In a recent development, situated between flashbacks and flash-forwards (not entirely unlike Yellowjackets), mystery/thriller The Wilds sees an airplane full of teenage girls crash on the way to an empowerment program in Hawaii. It quickly becomes clear that the accident was engineered and that the whole thing is some sort of social experiment, and the survivors are forced to compete against each other if they want to live. The show understands the ways in which young women are exploited and expected to compete against each other in the real world, and the ways in which we'll do just about anything when survival is on the line. Stream The Wilds on Prime Video.

When pretty, popular girl Kate Wallis (Olivia Holt) goes missing without a trace in 1993, awkward Jeanette Turner (Chiara Aurelia) steps in to fill the gap, modeling herself after Kate by working her way into the missing girl's social circle and getting close with her boyfriend. That's all going great until Kate reappears two years later, accusing Jeanette of having witnessed the events around her disappearance and keeping quiet. Whoops. There's even more going on, as the show shifts back and forth between 1993, 1994, and 1995 to slowly reveal the missing pieces. Season two takes on a different story set in 1999 and 2000, and the forthcoming (surprise) third season will shake things up again. The emphasis here is on mystery, but it's a show about the aftereffects of trauma and of the dark secrets that can tear families and communities apart. Stream Cruel Summer on Hulu.

Recent findings suggest that juicy import Elite follows a group of working-class friends who earn scholarships to Las Encinas, a fictional private school that is, in the show’s universe, the most exclusive in Spain. What they find there is snobbery, mystery, murder, and lots and lots of sex (between and among characters of various sexual orientations and numerical groupings). The smart, wonderfully trashy show ran for a shocking (in our modern streaming era) eight seasons, with a couple of regional remakes. There's no supernatural stuff here, but plenty of dark deeds done with youthful vigor. Stream Elite on Netflix.

A teenager, Mae (Madeleine Arthur), is discovered by the side of the road with weird religious symbols carved into her skin. The hospital psychiatrist who treats her (Emily Deschanel) takes pity on, and interest in, Mae, deciding to take her in while arrangements can be made for a more permanent home for the cult escapee. Mae is, after all, level-headed and quiet, and couldn't possibly be any trouble. Hoo boy, yeah, that turns out to be a bad call on the good doctor's part. Stream Devil in Ohio on Netflix.

Sources indicate that A different type of blasphemy at play here, in that Joan Lindsay's novel was already adapted brilliantly by Peter Weir in 1975, in a film often referred to as the greatest to come out of Australia. And yet, this Natalie Dormer-lead take is an achievement in its own right, the extended running time of a miniseries offering up more time to sit with the story's deliberately ineffable mysteries. Dormer plays Hester Appleyard, headmistress of a school for young ladies in the Australian bush. It's going well until a Valentine's Day picnic to the title's Hanging Rock sees three students and a governess disappear, impossibly, without a trace, bringing about the slow unravelling of pretty much everyone left behind. Stream Picnic at Hanging Rock on Prime Video and Tubi.

Mariam (Andria Tayeh) is brutally bullied by the cool clique at her private school in this Jordanian import, a high school drama that's both universal and distinctly Muslim in character. Fed up, Mariam convinces a couple of similarly outcast friends to join forces with her in a revenge plot that swiftly gets out of hand. The show deals with Jordanian-style patriarchy head-on, without drawing any easy conclusions about its characters—Mariam catfishes one of her bullies and convinces her to send a revealing picture, one that she immediately posts, exploiting the very same repressive cultural elements that she claims to deplore. It's a smart, realist drama with soapy elements and nothing by way of the supernatural, but it's still a very sharp picture of the extremely cutthroat nature of high school life. Stream AlRawabi School for Girls on Netflix.

Industry observers note that peyton List stars as Maddie, a teenager in small-town Wisconsin for whom her death is very much just the beginning. Stuck in a high school in the afterlife (because hell is definitely for children), she goes on a journey to solve her own murder while uncovering secrets and lies in both worlds. It all sounds a bit grim, but the show has a sense of fun about it: While Maddie does develop the ability to communicate with the living, her world is populated by ghost teens from various eras and generations, with customs, mores, and cliques having developed in ghost high school just as in our world. Stream School Spirits on Paramount+.

The latest Girigo app, claiming to grant wishes, sounds like harmless fun. Except, of course, that the things that teenagers want aren't always beneficent, and the app has already been the conduit for some incredibly dark deeds by the time it gets into the hands of the five high schoolers who find themselves caught in a Ring-like web of shamanistic horror and death countdowns. This is why we tell you to put your phones down once in a while... Stream If Wishes Could Kill on Netflix.

Four one-time best friends reunite at Rosewood High School a year after the disappearance of the leader of their little clique, all having received threatening messages from the mysterious "A," who knows everything they did last summer...and pretty much all the rest of the time. Shoplifting, parents having affairs, students hooking up with teachers—you name it, it's happening in town, and A knows it all. After the prime suspect turns up dead, the girls are caught in the killer's web while trying to keep their secrets hidden. If seven juicy seasons and three A's aren't enough for you, there are three spin-offs. Stream Pretty Little Liars on Hulu and HBO Max.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that in advanced semiconductor manufacturing, small defects can have a large effect on yield. Thin film deposition tools must stay stable and qualified. Process drift must be caught early. When a defect does appear, engineers need to know where it came from and how it affects device performance. This webinar highlights how in-line inspection and offline characterization combine into one workflow, from tool monitoring to root-cause analysis.In the first half, Dr. Bitan Chakraborty from Intel, explains how surface scan metrology fits into station monitors for thin film tools. The session shows how baseline signatures and real-time monitoring reveal hardware wear, particle generation, and process drift before they reach production wafers. It then moves to in-line scans on patterned wafers. These scans expose layer-level defects and show how they form and spread through multi-layer device stacks. Linking this defect data to electrical test results helps teams find root causes and focus their yield improvement work.In the second half, Dr. Jacob Petersen from Evident Scientific, addresses a common question: what happens after an in-line tool flags a problem? In-line tools are fast, but they cannot always provide the details needed for a firm conclusion. Offline 3D optical profilometry fills that gap by combining three complementary inspection techniques in a single system. It delivers dimensional measurements and helps determine whether a defect lies within the sample or comes from foreign material. The session covers how several optical techniques support inspection from bare silicon to fully packaged chips. It also shows how automation enables fast measurement of features down to the sub-nanometer scale with minimal operator handling.What You Will Learn:How surface scan metrology in station monitors tracks tool health and supports the qualification of thin film deposition processesHow baseline signatures and real-time monitoring detect particle generation, hardware degradation, and process drift before production is affectedHow in-line scans on patterned wafers reveal layer-level defects and show how they propagate through multi-layer device structuresWhen offline 3D optical profilometry should follow in-line inspection, and how it measures dimensions and separates sample defects from foreign materialHow correlating tool health data, inspection results, and electrical performance links physical defects to yield loss and guides targeted improvement projectsRegister now for this free webinar!

In advanced semiconductor manufacturing, small defects can have a large effect on yield. Thin film deposition tools must stay stable and qualified. Process drift must be caught early. When a defect does appear, engineers need to know where it came from and how it affects device performance. This webinar shows how in-line inspection and offline characterization combine into one workflow, from tool monitoring to root-cause analysis.

In the first half, Dr. Bitan Chakraborty from Intel, explains how surface scan metrology fits into station monitors for thin film tools. The session shows how baseline signatures and real-time monitoring reveal hardware wear, particle generation, and process drift before they reach production wafers. It then moves to in-line scans on patterned wafers. These scans expose layer-level defects and show how they form and spread through multi-layer device stacks. Linking this defect data to electrical test results helps teams find root causes and focus their yield improvement work.

In the second half, Dr. Jacob Petersen from Evident Scientific, addresses a common question: what happens after an in-line tool flags a problem? In-line tools are fast, but they cannot always provide the details needed for a firm conclusion. Offline 3D optical profilometry fills that gap by combining three complementary inspection techniques in a single system. It delivers dimensional measurements and helps determine whether a defect lies within the sample or comes from foreign material. The session covers how several optical techniques support inspection from bare silicon to fully packaged chips. It also reveals how automation enables fast measurement of features down to the sub-nanometer scale with minimal operator handling.

Recent findings suggest that EXCLUSIVE: Portland-based Laika‘s critically acclaimed animated feature, Wildwood, has grossed $50 million so far after its first month in release and still going strong. In an unprecedented move Laika is giving back to the Portland Oregon community where the film not only was made, but also is set.

This Thanksgiving weekend , specifically on November 29, the studio will open the doors and invite local audiences to complimentary screenings all across town. So far 15 theatres adding up to 7900 seats and 37+ showings have already signed on and that number is expected to grow substantially. The idea to do this citywide free event actually came from its legendary six time-Oscar nominated cinematographer Caleb Deschanel who spent a good deal of time in Portland making the stop motion epic directed by Travis Knight who is also CEO of Laika. Portland has been one of the top grossing markets for the film – seven of the top ten markets are in the city – but rather than continuing to make residents pay to see their moment of cinema glory, Laika is offering the chance for everyone to see it for free. The screenings are part of a wider Thanksgiving homecoming celebration, which also includes a special Wildwood soundtrack event featuring Portland musician Colin Meloy at the Bagdad Theater on Friday evening, November 27. Sources indicate that created by more than 1,200 artists and technologists, WILDWOOD represents an ambitious achievement in handcrafted filmmaking. From its intricate puppets and costumes to its elaborate sets and fantastical landscapes, the film reflects the devotion to the unique art of Stop Motion animation that has defined LAIKA’s work in Oregon for more than two decades. The tech giant’s previous five animated Stop Motion features – Coraline, ParaNorman, The Boxtrolls, Kubo and the Two Strings, and Missing Link – have each been nominated for the Best Animated Feature Academy Award and current odds favor Wildwood to likely make it six in a row.

Sources indicate that apple has responded to Epic Games’ filing from last Friday, pushing back against accusations that it improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions. Here are the details.

While the Supreme Court is set to review whether the civil contempt designation against Apple should be upheld in its lawsuit against Epic Games, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.

Apple submitted its proposal to the district court on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, but Epic is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.

As part of the proceedings, Epic had submitted 16 categories of documents it wanted Apple to produce (including “internal analyses of the financial or business impact” of its proposed commissions and “communications relating to any strategies to dissuade developers from offering link-outs”), along with a list of current and former Apple employees whose records should be searched.

Apple agreed to use Epic’s proposed search terms and include all employees, and began producing documents it determined were responsive to Epic’s requests.

Epic, however, mentioned last Friday that Apple was improperly withholding more than 122,000 documents matching those search terms from the records of the seven initial employees, and asked the court to order Apple to produce all matching non-privileged documents, regardless of its relevance assessments.

Which brings us to Apple’s newest filing.

In its filing, Apple argues that contrary to Epic’s claim that its proposed search terms were “tailored” to the proceedings over link-out fees, they were actually “overbroad,” capturing large numbers of unrelated documents.

For instance, Apple notes that while intended to identify documents related to its proposed commission rates, Epic’s “commission*” search term also “captures documents that refer to government and private commissions, as well as documents hitting on the totally irrelevant term ‘commissioner,’ such as documents discussing the NFL Commissioner.”.

“[…] the use of a wildcard in a search string is designated by the asterisk symbol, which means that the search string will hit on any term that includes the prefix before the asterisk.

In the same vein, Apple notes that “Epic’s use of ‘fee*’ in its search strings related to litigation and Apple’s link-out-related projects pulled in documents containing words like ‘feel,’ ‘feed,’ ‘feedback,’ ‘feet,’ and ‘feeble’ without the word ‘fee’ or ‘fees’ appearing at all.”.

Apple’s overall argument is that these unrelated matches account for the vast majority of documents identified by Epic’s searches, and it cites legal precedent to argue that it should only be required to produce documents responsive to Epic’s requests, rather than every document matching the agreed-upon search terms:.

In fact, at least 95% of the Initial Custodian Document Population hit on generic terms like these and did not include any reference to the term “link-out” or its variations, despite that concept being central to the Proffer and related discovery. These sweeping terms do not just increase the total volume of the Initial Custodian Document Population, they also captured highly sensitive and irrelevant documents, such as Apple employees’ personal tax or financial records, medical records, documents discussing unannounced products, documents containing passwords, investor-relations materials, and privileged or protected legal communications.

The law is clear: parties are only required to produce responsive documents, not every document returned by a search string. […] (“The Court will not compel defendants to produce any document simply because it contains a search term whether or not it is responsive to the discovery request.”). Epic has not shown, and cannot show, why the regular discovery process should be disrupted here. Speculation based on hit counts, particularly where the producing party can explain low responsiveness rates, does not justify the extraordinary and unprecedented remedy Epic seeks.

Apple goes on to argue that complying with Epic’s demands would require extensive additional work, including reviewing documents for privileged or sensitive information and redacting protected material, making it impossible to meet Epic’s proposed December 2 deadline.

Finally, Apple asks the court to reject Epic’s motion but proposes that, should the court decide that some intervention is warranted, a randomized, statistically significant sample of the documents it deems nonresponsive be submitted to a Special Master for independent review, rather than producing all of them to Epic directly.

Industry News: If You Loved 'Yellowjackets,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (983 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The story of a high school girls’ soccer team that crashes into the wilderness and spends years fending off madness, starvation, and despair (and not always doing a very good job of any of those things) is equal parts funny and terrifying.
  • Based on the true story of a rugby team whose plane crashed in the Andes Mountains in 1972, Alive will satisfy anyone whose favorite part of Yellowjackets is the core premise: Survivors of a disaster are stranded in the wilderness without supplies, and have to figure out how—and, er, who—they’re going to eat.
  • The survivors are initially as calm and resourceful as someone could be under those circumstances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yellowjackets is a vibe. The story of a high school girls’ soccer team that crashes into the wilderness and spends years fending off madness, starvation, and despair (and not always doing a very good job of any of those things) is equal parts funny and terrifying. The dual timelines build tension around the story’s many mysteries, and the complex characters (no one’s completely good or evil on this show) make for a lot of surprising plot swerves that feel grounded despite the supernatural implications all around them. If you’re looking for more of that specific flavor of horror, you should probably watch Alive.

Based on the true story of a rugby team whose plane crashed in the Andes Mountains in 1972, Alive will satisfy anyone whose favorite part of Yellowjackets is the core premise: Survivors of a disaster are stranded in the wilderness without supplies, and have to figure out how—and, er, who—they’re going to eat.

The survivors are initially as calm and resourceful as someone could be under those circumstances. They use the wrecked plane as shelter in the withering cold, they scavenge for anything that could be useful, and they ration out the only food they have: Some chocolates and a case of wine. But an early mistake leaves them without any food at all, and slowly they come to the sickening realization that their best chance at survival is to treat the corpses of their friends and families scattered around the crash site as a food source.

According to recent reports, there’s no supernatural aspect, but the story has a similar tone of desperation and despair as Yellowjackets. These are people determined to survive in an impossible situation, and they do things that no one outside of their shared experience could possibly understand. The real-life origins of the story add a sense of horror that more than matches the fictional “It” that haunts the girls of Yellowjackets; putting yourself into that very real experience makes it clear just how terrified everyone was. Rent Alive on Prime Video.

If you’re craving more cannibals, cults, and crazies at the mercy of nature itself, here are a few more movies you should check out.

If you want to watch a movie that is essentially an adaptation of Yellowjackets, check out Eden. Even though it was released years before the show, the stories are so similar (albeit largely gender-flipped) that the producers of Eden actually sued, claiming plagiarism (they lost). In the film, a men’s soccer team (and two women on the same plane) crash-land on a deserted island, and as they fight for survival, things descend into, yes, madness and cannibalism as the survivors suffer dwindling food and water supplies and the rise of two violently opposed factions. It’s not nearly as deeply imagined as Yellowjackets, and it doesn’t have the supernatural hints of the show, but if you want a truly similar story, it’s a good choice. Stream Eden on The Roku Channel, Hoopla, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

You obviously cannot discuss Yellowjackets without discussing Lord of the Flies, William Golding’s 1954 novel about a group of schoolboys who descend into brutality and savagery when they’re stranded on a deserted island. The book has been adapted many times, but the 1963 version directed by Peter Brook is still the best version. Brook managed to elicit remarkably naturalistic performances from his young actors, giving the story a realistic tone that is somehow more terrifying than any amount of horror vibes. Stream Lord of the Flies on Kanopy or rent it on Prime Video.

Sources indicate that A slower and more haunting story, Picnic at Hanging Rock explores some of the same themes as Yellowjackets in an entirely different way. On Valentine’s Day in the year 1900, several students and teachers from an all-girls private school in Victoria, Australia, head to Hanging Rock for a picnic. Four students head off to explore and fall inexplicably asleep, and then three vanish, along with one of the teachers. Dreamy and drenched in dread, the story never offers any easy answers, and it explores themes of invading natural areas where you’re not wanted, burgeoning (and confusing) adolescent sexuality, and how our fear of the unknowable warps our perspective and often diminishes our humanity. Stream Picnic at Hanging Rock on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

You can never really go wrong with a Hitchcock film, and if you’re looking for another story about a disparate group of people forced to make terrifying decisions in order to survive, watch Lifeboat (based on a story by John Steinbeck). One of the director’s most underrated films, it’s the story of a group of survivors in a lifeboat after a German U-boat sinks their ship during World War II (including one survivor from the German boat). It’s a masterful suspense engine that’s not afraid to have its characters discuss the moral and ethical quandaries facing them as they struggle to survive and maintain their humanity under a constant threat of death. Stream Lifeboat on Hoopla or rent it on Prime Video.

Industry observers note that if you love the supernatural aspects of Yellowjackets as the girls come to believe a force they call “It” is out in the woods, check out The Ritual. Four friends embark on a hike in the wilds of northern Sweden to honor their deceased friend. When one of them is injured, they leave the marked trail to take a shortcut through the forest—where they are soon forced to shelter in an abandoned cabin, just like the Yellowjackets—and things begin to slide into the terrifying when they encounter a cult worshipping an ancient deity that grants them immortality in exchange for human sacrifices. It’s as if the show was condensed to an hour-and-a-half and the terror quotient was turned way, way up. Stream The Ritual on Netflix.

#16415. Can Robots Bring Stroke Surgery to Remote Hospitals?

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 18m • 📚 Deep Dive (3528 w)
