💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that popular secure messaging app Signal has rolled out a fresh update that automatically disables screenshots for the sake of blocking Siri AI from reading your chats.
  • Signal’s latest app revision on iPhone disables a key system feature: taking screenshots.
  • As Signal told Reuters, that’s because Apple doesn’t right now provide better tools for iOS developers to safeguard app content from Siri AI and third-party AI agents.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that popular secure messaging app Signal has rolled out a fresh update that automatically disables screenshots for the sake of blocking Siri AI from reading your chats. Here are the details.

Signal’s latest app revision on iPhone disables a key system feature: taking screenshots.

As Signal told Reuters, that’s because Apple doesn’t right now provide better tools for iOS developers to safeguard app content from Siri AI and third-party AI agents.

By default, users who update and try to take a screenshot will see a message that says: “Screenshot prevented by ‘Block Siri AI’ setting.”.

Sources indicate that fortunately, there’s an easy workaround. People who want to re-enable screenshots can do so by visiting Signal’s privacy settings and turning off the upcoming toggle that’s labeled ‘Block Siri AI.’.

Here’s 9to5Mac’s own Arin Waichulis:.

Signal now blocks in-app screenshots on iPhone to keep Siri AI from reading chatsIt’s a new toggle in settings that’s on by default, but can be turned offNo equivalent for its Mac app pic.twitter.com/ImsinqMNPq.

Here’s exactly what that toggle does, per the in-app settings:.

In a recent development, prevent Siri AI from scanning Signal content. This will also block you from taking screenshots in the app and App Switcher.

It’s good to see that consumers can manually disable the upcoming privacy setting if they want. But Signal’s decision to block screenshots does raise notable questions about the potential gap in privacy tools for iOS developers.

Apple already lets you block Siri AI from accessing whichever apps you manually exclude, and that became even easier in iOS 27.2. But rather than directing people to that system option, Signal seems to believe it needed to take action itself with this update.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

New titles land on Netflix so often that the hardest part of movie night isn't making the popcorn; it’s deciding what to actually watch. It’s all too easy to get caught in the "what to watch" trap, especially when the streamer’s November 2026 slate hasn't let up, adding 51 movies at the start of the month and even more every single week.

With the weekend rolling around again, we here at Tom’s Guide want to save you the endless scrolling and have pulled together three fresh arrivals worth your time. Whether you’re a horror fan ready for the latest chilling installment of a long-running supernatural franchise, in the mood for a heartfelt road-trip dramedy starring Robert De Niro and Bobby Cannavale, or eager to start the Christmas countdown early (ugh, really?) with a holiday comedy that reunites the Lawrence brothers, we've got you covered.

That lineup should keep you busy over the next couple of days, and you might just come away with a upcoming favorite. Here are three new-to-Netflix movies to add to your weekend watchlist.

It has been revealed that bobby Cannavale has built a career on brash, combustible live wires, but “Ezra” makes for one of his most tender performances by far. He's a father who’ll risk everything for his autistic son in this movie, and knows how to tug on those heartstrings.

It has been revealed that directed by Tony Goldwyn (“Conviction,” “A Walk on the Moon”), this flick follows Max Bernal (Cannavale), a stand-up comic who’s torched his career and his marriage and moved back in with his father, Stan (Robert De Niro). Life is hardly going the way he planned, but somehow he's getting through it.

In a recent development, when doctors want to medicate his young son Ezra (William A. Fitzgerald) and move him to a special school as a way to "treat" his autism, Max makes a reckless call and takes the boy on an unplanned cross-country road trip instead, hoping to bring about some changes in the pair's lives.

According to recent reports, watch "Ezra" on Netflix on Nov. 20.

The Lawrence brothers made their names on ’90s TV, from Joey’s “whoa”-laden performance on “Blossom” to Matthew’s appearance on “Boy Meets World,” and they've reunited for the holiday comedy “Marry Christmas.”.

Directed by Andrew Lawrence, the film casts Joey and Matthew Lawrence as the Wright brothers (no, not those), two newly engaged siblings who realize they’ve booked the same venue for competing weddings on Christmas Day. A rivalry breaks out over which brother gets to tie the knot on the holiday.

It has been revealed that if you want a feel-good '90s-inspired comedy that gives all the Lawrence brothers a chance to feel like they're really doing something, this is it. And you'll have a good time bopping along with the two grooms while thinking about Christmas during simpler times.

It has been revealed that watch "Marry Christmas" on Netflix starting Nov. 21.

The "Insidious" franchise spent five films and more than a decade haunting the Lambert family, but its sixth chapter, “Insidious: Out of the Further,” hands the nightmares to someone entirely new. That's good news if you haven't gotten caught up with the movies just yet.

Directed by Jacob Chase (“Come Play”), this entry stars Amelia Eve as Gemma, a mother raising her daughter in the house she grew up in, who discovers she can cross into the Further, the realm of lost souls at the heart of the series.

In a recent development, once the demons work out what she can do, our world becomes their playground. Franchise mainstay Lin Shaye returns as parapsychologist Elise Rainier, but otherwise this is a pretty good entry point for anyone who wants to see what all the fuss is about.

Watch "Insidious: Out of the Further" on Netflix on Nov. 21.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27 gives the Messages app a variety of welcome upgrades, including one I’ve found myself using a lot: a Smart Reply feature that’s now personalized to the user’s writing style.

When the first wave of Apple Intelligence features were declared in 2024, one that I immediately thought sounded useful was Smart Reply.

The idea behind Smart Reply is simple. Rather than needing to manually type out replies in Messages and Mail, your iPhone can offer prewritten replies you can choose and send with a couple taps.

Great in theory, but the ‘Smart’ part of Smart Reply struggled to materialize in iOS 18.

Fortunately, with a key Apple Intelligence upgrade in iOS 27, the newly introduced version of the feature finally lives up to its name. Per Apple:.

Smart Reply in Mail and Messages can now draw on a user’s personalized writing style.

Before, Smart Reply would look at the context of a conversation to craft its suggestions. But now, it also aims to match your writing style, punctuation, and tone.

In iOS 18, I almost never used Smart Reply. That’s because despite being fine at suggesting replies that technically worked, those suggestions didn’t sound like me at all.

Industry observers note that that’s changed in iOS 27. Smart Reply now consistently impresses me. It no longer offers generic responses that sound like AI wrote them. Instead, its suggestions actually fit with my normal style of communication.

According to recent reports, the only drawback is that right now, you’ll only ever see two Smart Reply suggestions. If Apple expanded the feature by letting you scroll horizontally through more options, I suspect I’d use Smart Reply even more.

Have you been using iOS 27’s Smart Reply feature in Messages? Let us know in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, we don't know about you, but with the chaos of the holidays coming up, the last thing we want is to waste precious brain cells trying to decide what to watch next. That's where Tom's Guide comes in: We do the work of regularly sifting through the best streaming services and their seemingly endless options of new movies and television demonstrates, and compile an easy, breezy TV guide of what exactly you should be clicking "Play" on a given weekend.

And this weekend is no exception: We've sorted through what's recently arrived on Netflix, HBO Max, Paramount Plus, and more and narrowed things down to a trio of great watches, one for each night of your weekend.

Sources indicate that on Friday evening, you can hang out with "The Altruists"; the Netflix true-crime drama centers on the biggest crypto fraud in history. Consider Saturday a pseudo date night with one of the world's most legendary chefs, with the HBO Max premiere of the Anthony Bourdain biopic, "Tony." And a lazy Sunday sounds like the perfect day to catch up with the ladies of "Yellowjackets," as the survival thriller kicks off its fourth and final season this week.

It has been revealed that that's a solid weekend of streaming sorted, no? All you have to do is grab some snacks and the remote.

If you love tech-world dramas like "The Dropout," "The Audacity" and "Super Pumped: The Battle for Uber," you'll likely enjoy "The Altruists," a true-crime saga centered on the whirlwind rise and catastrophic collapse of the multi-billion-dollar crypto exchange FTX, which premiered on Netflix on Thursday, November 19.

Starring Anthony Boyle as FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried and three-time Emmy winner Julia Garner as Caroline Ellison—the CEO of FTX's sister hedge fund Alameda Research and Sam's on-and-off-again girlfriend—the eight-part limited series follows the couple's transformation from ambitious young idealists trying to revolutionize the finance world to culprits in an $8 billion scheme that upended the entire crypto market.

The stacked ensemble cast includes Alex Lawther, Karan Soni, Matt Rife, Madison Hu, Paul Reiser, Jennifer Grey, Robin Weigert and "Heated Rivalry" star Hudson Williams.

Stream "The Altruists" on Netflix now.

If you don't know him for his cooking, then you do for his cool: The late, great Anthony Bourdain was one of the most singular figures to come out of the culinary world, so it's no surprise that he'd be the subject of a high-profile bio-drama.

According to recent reports, but instead of charting Bourdain's days as a hotshot chef in top New York kitchens, this Matt Johnson-directed biopic takes it back to the toque's beginnings as an impulsive 19-year-old (played by "The Holdovers" standout Dominic Sessa) working a summer dishwasher job at a local restaurant in 1970s Provincetown, Massachusetts. Under the tutelage of Chef José Vatel (Antonio Banderas) and the gritty restaurant crew, Tony B. gets his first real taste of the chaos and triumphs of a professional kitchen.

The A24 flick—which also stars Emilia Jones, Leo Woodall, Stavros Halkias, and real-life chef icon Eric Ripert—will make its subscription streaming debut on HBO Max on Saturday, November 20.

It has been revealed that the final chapter of "Yellowjackets" is finally here, with the survival drama's fourth season premiering on Paramount+ on Friday, November 20. But if you, like yours truly, are a bit behind on the psychological thriller, a long Sunday catching up with the unhinged antics of Shauna (played by Sophie Nélisse in the past and Melanie Lynskey in the present), Taissa (Jasmin Savoy Brown and Tawny Cypress), Misty (Samantha Hanratty and Christina Ricci) and the rest of the gang sounds like a day well spent.

If you're not familiar, "Yellowjackets" follows a 1996 high school girls' soccer team in the aftermath of a plane crash, which leaves them stranded deep in the remote Canadian wilderness. Their fight for survival descends into a psychological nightmare as the girls begin dabbling in ritualized cannibalism, group hunts, and other cultish mysticism. In a parallel timeline set in the present day, the adult survivors must reckon with those dark secrets and long-held regrets 25 years later.

Stream "Yellowjackets" on Paramount+ now.

The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor fixes that with a light sensor most motion sensors lack, along with mmWave radar.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.

According to recent reports, A standard motion sensor uses PIR, which only detects movement, and that works fine in many situations. If you’re still for long periods, you’re invisible, and the automation assumes the room is empty. The Lafaer LWR02 pairs PIR with 2.4 GHz mmWave radar. The PIR-based motion sees you walking in, and the radar sees the minor stuff, like breathing and shifting on the couch, so the room stays “occupied” for as long as you are in it. The two together also reduce false positives from ceiling fans, curtains, and the dog, because the radar and PIR both must agree before the sensor reports motion.

In Apple Home, that demonstrates up as an occupancy sensor and a motion sensor from the same device.

“Turn on the lights when someone enters” is a common automation I use, but it can be tricky. What if you only want it when it’s not light outside? Doing it based on time of day sometimes works, but what about depending on where the windows are facing, etc.? You might have a room that gets darker an hour earlier than another room. “Turn on the lights when someone enters, and it’s dark in the room” is what the light sensor can handle for you.

In the Home app, that means triggering a sensor for occupancy, then converting the automation into a Shortcut and adding a condition for the light level. It’s a few extra steps, but it does really give you more fine control over how it works.

Presence, motion, light, temperature, and humidity all come from the same device, and each one appears in Apple Home as its own sensor, so you can build automations around whichever ones fit the room.

According to recent reports, it’s IPX3-rated, so bathrooms, kitchens, and laundry rooms are fine to use in. Coverage is about 13 feet for presence and 26 for motion across about 120 degrees, which works in a bedroom, office, or bathroom. It’s not going to cover a great room from one corner. The base is a magnetic half sphere, so you can aim it, and it mounts with adhesive or sits on a shelf. I generally like to use the shelf for these types of sensors.

Sources indicate that the Lafaer LWR02 is Matter over Thread, so it pairs directly with a HomePod, HomePod mini, or Apple TV 4K with no Lafaer hub or account needed. It runs on two included AAA batteries, is rated for up to two years, and rechargeable AAAs work with it as well. Thread is why a sensor doing this much can last that long on batteries. All sensor data is processed locally, so it only uses a trickle on the batteries.

Sources indicate that lights that turn off while you’re sitting still in the room are the reason a lot of people stop using motion automations in smart homes. The Lafaer LWR02 fixes that with mmWave radar and then lets you have more granular control of light-based automations based on what’s actually in the environment in the room, not just the time of day.

The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor is available on Amazon.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, airPods 5 were introduced in September and come in two different versions.
  • Recent findings suggest that the case for the higher-end AirPods 5 ($149) supports wireless charging and Find My.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The holiday shopping season is here, and Apple’s AirPods are sure to be one of the most popular gifts. If you’re shopping for AirPods, Apple sells three different models: AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 3, and AirPods Max 2. Here’s how they compare.

In a recent development, airPods 5 were introduced in September and come in two different versions. Unlike their predecessors, both versions of AirPods 5 offer Active Noise Cancellation. They differ in the charging case, battery life, and volume control. The base model AirPods 5 ($129) come with a case that can only charge via USB-C.

Recent findings suggest that the case for the higher-end AirPods 5 ($149) supports wireless charging and Find My. You also get one extra hour of battery life. The higher-end model also adds on-stem volume control, so you can adjust the volume just by swiping up or down on one of the earbud stems.

Here’s a full comparison between both AirPods 5 models:.

The key thing about AirPods 5 is their open-ear design, unlike the in-ear design of the AirPods Pro 3 (more on those later). Even with that open-ear design, AirPods 5 offer incredible Active Noise Cancellation capabilities.

It has been revealed that if you are shopping for AirPods 5, I do recommend spending the extra $20 to get the higher-end model. The better charging case alone is worth the extra money. With Find My integration and a built-in speaker, you can track your AirPods and play a sound from the case if you lose them.

If the person you’re shopping for doesn’t like in-ear earbuds, AirPods 5 are an excellent choice.

For most people, though, AirPods Pro 3 are probably the better choice ….

It has been revealed that airPods Pro 3 are Apple’s most capable earbuds, even with the introduction of AirPods 5 this year. They offer an in-ear fit and come with five foam-infused silicone ear tip sizes. With that in-ear design, AirPods Pro 3 can offer up to 3x stronger noise cancellation than AirPods 5. In my testing, this difference is notable.

AirPods Pro 3 also offer several other features you won’t find on AirPods 5, including a heart rate sensor for workouts, plus Hearing Test, Hearing Aid, and Hearing Protection features.

In a recent development, I still think AirPods Pro 3 are one of the best products in Apple’s lineup today. I wear mine for multiple hours every single day and can’t imagine life without them. I love the in-ear fit, and the ANC still impresses me, whether I’m at home or somewhere like a coffee shop.

If you know the person you’re shopping for (whether it’s yourself or someone else) likes the in-ear earbud design, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option. This is especially true when AirPods Pro 3 are on sale, like they are right now at $179. The price difference between AirPods 5 and AirPods Pro 3 is very small, and you’re getting a much better product.

It has been revealed that finally, we have AirPods Max. These are Apple’s only option for people who want AirPods in an over-ear headphone form factor. Last year, they were pretty hard to recommend since they’d gone five years without a real upgrade.

In a recent development, this year, however, Apple officially introduced AirPods Max 2, bringing modern features to Apple’s high-end headphones. This includes features like Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, Personalized Volume, and more.

AirPods Max 2 are a far more compelling option than AirPods Max were at this time last year. They’re still pricey, but I love the aesthetics and find them very comfortable. There’s something about the premium aluminum design with an elegant Digital Crown that really stands out.

According to recent reports, if you’re looking to splurge this holiday season, AirPods Max 2 are a great choice. For more realistic budgets, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option.

According to recent reports, are you planning to buy anyone AirPods this holiday season? Are they on your wishlist? Let us know down in the comments.

Ripple Is Rapidly Expanding the Potential Use Cases for Its Stablecoin. Here's Why That's Bearish for XRP.

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (589 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ripple had a substantial week in late October, striking deals with Robinhood and Coinbase to support its stablecoin, Ripple USD (RLUSD +0.00%).
  • Sources indicate that with that in mind, Ripple USD's success may seem like good news for XRP.
  • 27, Robinhood announced Ripple USD was live on Robinhood Chain and Bitstamp, the cryptocurrency exchange it acquired last year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lyle Daly – Nov 20, 2026 at 11:30AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than XRP ›.

Ripple had a substantial week in late October, striking deals with Robinhood and Coinbase to support its stablecoin, Ripple USD (RLUSD +0.00%). The blockchain organization is also the largest holder of XRP (XRP -7.44%), and CEO Brad Garlinghouse has said that XRP and stablecoins like Ripple USD are complementary rather than competitive.

Sources indicate that with that in mind, Ripple USD's success may seem like good news for XRP. I'm not convinced; these deals look more like XRP getting left behind.

On Oct. 27, Robinhood announced Ripple USD was live on Robinhood Chain and Bitstamp, the cryptocurrency exchange it acquired last year. It will be available in the Robinhood app later this year. Robinhood will use Ripple USD on the XRP Ledger (XRPL) to settle institutional trades on Bitstamp, and it will integrate Ripple Treasury into its global treasury operations.

Industry observers note that A day later, Ripple and Coinbase announced a partnership, with the crypto exchange making Ripple USD available on Coinbase Prime, Coinbase Exchange, and the Coinbase Retail app. Coinbase Global Exchange customers will eventually be able to use the stablecoin as collateral.

Industry observers note that the problem for XRP holders is that Ripple USD isn't reliant on the cryptocurrency or its blockchain. About 74% of the Ripple USD supply is on Ethereum, according to DeFiLlama data from Nov. 19, compared to 25% on the XRPL and the rest on other blockchains. Coinbase's stablecoin integration supports Ethereum, Base, and XRPL.

In a recent development, in fairness, there's still a sizable amount of Ripple USD on the XRPL, and it's nearly 90% of the blockchain's total stablecoin supply. XRP is the native cryptocurrency on the XRPL and is used to pay transaction fees. However, this is where the network's low fees can be a double-edged sword. Transaction fees start at 0.00001 XRP, meaning even Ripple USD activity doesn't generate much demand for XRP.

CRYPTO · As of 2:20 PM ET 11/20/26.

An even deeper issue is that Ripple USD cannibalizes XRP's primary use case. The pitch for XRP is that it can serve as a bridge currency for financial institutions to send and receive cross-border payments. But a stablecoin pegged at $1 works much better as a bridge currency than a volatile cryptocurrency like XRP. The more Ripple USD grows, the less XRP is needed.

Ripple USD is having a successful 2026, going from a market cap of $1.3 billion at the start of the year to $2.8 billion as of Nov. 18, becoming one of the 10 largest stablecoins in the process. XRP, on the other hand, has plummeted from a market cap of $122 billion in January to $63 billion. Institutional demand has fallen, with spot XRP ETFs losing $19.1 million in the week ending Nov. 13, the largest weekly outflow in eight months.

It has been revealed that the partnerships with Robinhood and Coinbase show that Ripple is building a legitimate stablecoin business. That's good for Ripple and Ripple USD, but the success doesn't flow back to XRP.

#16336. 5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1178 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Zdnet ↗ Open Full Page

5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1178 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that at the beginning of the year, few organizations were utilizing large language models (LLMs) and AI agents in their cybersecurity workflows, including for discovering and patching vulnerabilities.
  • Also: Rogue AI incidents hit ‘tens of thousands’: Can businesses trust these tools?
  • According to recent reports, the capabilities of agentic AI are fast outstripping the speed and scale at which traditional security operations centers (SOCs) can operate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that at the beginning of the year, few organizations were utilizing large language models (LLMs) and AI agents in their cybersecurity workflows, including for discovering and patching vulnerabilities. According to Google, this is now happening at scale.

Also: Rogue AI incidents hit ‘tens of thousands’: Can businesses trust these tools?

According to recent reports, the capabilities of agentic AI are fast outstripping the speed and scale at which traditional security operations centers (SOCs) can operate. Like it or not, AI has an integral role in the new reality — for the defenders and threat actors.

In a recent development, speed and scale are the main reasons enterprises consider adopting AI in SOCs and for security more broadly, and these factors underpin Google’s upcoming security forecast for 2027 — Cloud CISO Perspectives. However, without the right precautions, AI security adopters could inadvertently increase their attack surface rather than shrink it.

With this in mind, these are five ways AI will change the security industry over the next year and what CISOs need to consider going into 2027.

Recent findings suggest that alert fatigue is well-known across SOC teams. Alert after alert needs to be trawled through; many are irrelevant or false positives, tying up skilled staff with the mundane, tedious, time-consuming task of triaging them.

Now that autonomous, AI-driven threats can probe a network, gain entry, and move laterally across it in minutes, chasing threat data and security alerts from multiple systems logged days or weeks ago can’t help a business mitigate them — and certainly not at the speed of the threat.

In a recent development, according to Google’s forecast, AI will mean the alert queue quietly disappears. Ramya Chitrakar, VP of engineering at Google Cloud Security, believes that “2027 is the year analysts stop chasing alerts and start shaping outcomes.”.

Also: AI is both a cyber weapon and a massive target.

According to recent reports, how? CISOs must change the alert model itself. Instead of human defenders triaging alerts at the start of a cybersecurity incident, the alert becomes final output, with autonomous agents handling “data enrichment, correlation, and triage automatically, surfacing a verified conclusion rather than a raw ticket,” according to Google.

This means cybersecurity experts can oversee alert handling and verify automated actions, potentially freeing them to focus on other tasks.

Custom agentic AI is often designed — or at least intended — to work autonomously, with human oversight. However, having thousands of individual agents working across multiple environments can create high-value entry points into corporate networks that cyberattackers target.

We need to think of agentic AI as more than a tool: each one needs its own identity, like a human employee, to operate within a zero-trust architecture, retain control, and reduce the risk of compromise.

Also: Your enterprise AI access can be sold for pennies – beware ‘LLM Mixers’.

Industry observers note that however, Heather Adkins, VP of security engineering at Google, thinks this needs to go further and suggests the zero-trust concept shouldn’t stop at the network layer. Instead, Adkins believes it needs to reach the transaction layer.

A paper trail for each agent needs to be established, which is impossible to handle manually, and even within a zero-trust framework, AI agents could be given too much scope. Instead, implement verification for each transaction and for every authorization, and assign each AI agent its own least-privilege set of credentials that can be revoked if there is a security incident or the agent is no longer required.

“When backed by real-time autonomous reasoning, we can dynamically allow a transaction on Tuesday and block the exact same request on Wednesday if conditions look anomalous,” the report notes.

AI is being used to speed up the development and deployment of newly introduced software, and in 2027, security will have to become a continuous system embedded in the software delivery pipeline, according to Google.

Threat actors have carried out software supply chain attacks over the years, one of the most notable being the SolarWinds incident of 2020. Sandra Joyce, VP of Google Threat Intelligence, states cybercriminals are now poisoning everything from open-source code to software libraries, which AI coding assistants often pull automatically into codebases.

Also: How AI security failures are endangering your supply chain.

It has been revealed that bug-fix tickets that take days to respond to and security appearing at the end of a software development cycle no longer work. Instead, writing and securing code must happen simultaneously, with the help of agentic AI, so speed doesn’t compromise security.

“It’s also crucial that we link live production environments directly back to source code so that defenders can trace a real-world exposure to the exact line of code, validate whether it is genuinely exploitable, and deliver a pre-tested fix at machine speed without breaking production,” Google added.

As organizations rush to implement AI into their applications and services to appear “AI-first,” innovative, and modern, security may be ignored or treated as an afterthought.

As a result, we may face a upcoming, broader attack surface than we realize, as AI introduces new security concerns, including software vulnerabilities, misconfiguration, bypasses, and indirect prompt injection attacks. Now that AI is also in the hands of all cyberattackers — from script kiddies to state-sponsored groups — auditing corporate networks and infrastructure is crucial.

In a recent development, also: Who’s responsible for catching rogue AI agents? You are.

Penetration testing and red team exercises now need to cover agentic AI. This wasn’t in scope for many red teams only a few years ago, but now that businesses have run with the idea of implementing AI in their workflows, processes, and products, organizations need to identify and fix security concerns introduced by AI before threat actors take advantage of them.

CISOs should task pen testers with auditing before an autonomous workflow hits production, then combine the results with threat intelligence to ensure defenders have the information they need to bolster network defenses and harden classifiers against upcoming and novel attacks.

The final significant trend we are likely to see in 2027 is tackling agent sprawl to create coordinated teams of AI agents that can rapidly handle security tasks at scale.

Single AI agents given general instructions won’t cut it when AI-assisted attackers can compromise endpoint devices, enter networks, move laterally, or start stealing data in a far shorter timeframe than before. Instead, CISOs should replace these “generalist” AI agents with specialized, orchestrated teams of AI agents that can meet the demands of defending against AI-driven attacks by employing specialist tooling and skill sets.

Also: AI agent kill switch urged by Okta-led alliance.

According to recent reports, CISOs also need to ensure that each agent has its own domain training and understanding, memory, and dedicated tools, and can act on its own within set limits, with a central coordinator that knows when to hand a decision to a human. This requires oversight, but in return, organizations will avoid agent sprawl, which the tech giant believes is the next iteration of shadow IT and its associated threats.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple is exploring how people use AI for their health, presumably to build its own AI health coach. On Sunday, it debuted the Apple Health AI Usage Study, which could contribute to the next AI health experience Apple builds by measuring the quality of AI health responses, comprehension, and everyday health behaviors, according to a press release.

Industry observers note that apple is conducting the study in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform widely used by healthcare professionals. The study examines the relationship between conversational AI tools, like chatbots, and the people who use them.

“Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey,” Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness, said in the press release.

Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for.

In a recent development, participants are encouraged to share their HealthKit data and query the health app with questions. The study will also explore how AI tools can best prepare patients ahead of clinical visits. Apple will monitor the AI’s clarity and approachability when providing medical information, and each response or recommendation will be linked to peer-reviewed clinical citations. Responses could be unclear or incomplete, which is why Apple is rolling this out as a study to explore a responsibly designed AI health assistant.

Recent findings suggest that apple often rolls out studies for features it would like to develop in the future. For example, many of the hearing health features launched on the AirPods were a direct result of the findings from Apple’s Hearing Study.

Also: Athenahealth patients can ask Claude about their medical records now.

Recent findings suggest that the AI usage study comes on the heels of the revamped Health app’s debut, which introduces officially next month. It also arrives amid a bevy of AI health coaches, popping up alongside companion health devices. Google released its AI Health Coach in Google Health Premium last year, and Oura launched a proprietary AI model for women trained on medical standards and research from Oura’s in-house team of board-certified clinicians.

A growing number of Americans are relying on AI for medical advice. A recent survey from Pew Research Center found that 34% of US adults have talked with a chatbot for medical advice. As AI proliferates, that percentage will only increase.

“Patients and clinicians are both turning to AI, but the tools they use are being built and tested in separate worlds,” stated Robert M. Wachter, M.D., UCSF’s professor and chair of the Department of Medicine, in the press release.

Apple and other tech companies are building for this newly introduced health normal, and the AI usage study indicates that Apple isn’t taking the responsibility lightly.

Industry observers note that if you’re interested in participating in Apple’s study, it’s open to 200,000 eligible participants age 21 and older in the US. You’ll need a phone with Apple Intelligence enabled (the iPhone 15 Pro or later), running iOS 26 or later. You can download the study app to learn more and enroll.

  • As space exploration needs evolve, investors often weigh defense stability against rapid disruption.
  • Lockheed Martin serves as a cornerstone of national security by providing advanced aircraft and missile systems to global governments.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Brendan Coffey – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 11:30AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Lockheed Martin ›.

As space exploration needs evolve, investors often weigh defense stability against rapid disruption. Choosing between Lockheed Martin (LMT -0.28%) and Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -6.19%) depends on your appetite for risk versus consistent performance.

Lockheed Martin serves as a cornerstone of national security by providing advanced aircraft and missile systems to global governments. Space Exploration Technologies--SpaceX-- focuses on reusable rockets and global satellite internet through its Starlink program. Both companies are central to the future of aerospace, making them a natural match-up for long-term retail investors.

In its latest annual report, filed for the most recent period, Lockheed Martin highlights its role as a premier global security company. It relies heavily on government contracts, with nearly 72% of its 2025 sales coming from agencies of the U.S. federal government. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, as revenue depends on federal budget priorities.

Reliable recent quarterly figures for at least one of these companies aren't available, so this comparison uses each organization's latest full fiscal year. In FY 2025, the company reported revenue of about $75.1 billion, representing growth of approximately 5.7% over the previous year. This revenue supported a net income of roughly $5.0 billion, which reflects the company's ability to remain profitable despite complex global supply chains.

Sources indicate that as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is around 7.9x, indicating that the tech giant uses a significant amount of borrowed money compared to shareholder equity. The current ratio, which measures the ability to cover short-term obligations with current assets, is approximately 1.1x. For the same fiscal year, the company generated free cash flow of about $6.9 billion, providing ample room for shareholder returns among defense stocks.

During FY 2025, revenue reached about $18.7 billion, which was a sharp increase of roughly 33% compared to the prior year. Despite this rapid top-line growth, the firm reported a net loss of about $4.9 billion. This underscores the high costs associated with developing next-generation spacecraft and expanding a global satellite constellation.

According to recent reports, the company's December 2025 balance sheet reveals a debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 0.6x, suggesting a relatively lower reliance on debt relative to its equity. Its current ratio is close to 1.4x, signifying a healthy cushion for meeting short-term financial needs. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC) represented roughly 28.7% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement. Free cash flow for the period was a negative $14.0 billion.

It has been revealed that lockheed Martin faces significant risks from its revenue concentration, as nearly 72% of its 2025 sales came from the U.S. federal government. Any shifts in defense priorities or budget cuts could impact its long-term contracts. Furthermore, the F-35 program accounts for roughly 27% of total revenue, meaning any technical failures for that specific aircraft would be damaging. The organization also navigates intense competition from peers like RTX Corp. (RTX -0.20%) for high-stakes government projects.

Recent findings suggest that space Exploration Technologies operates in a capital-intensive industry where regulatory changes can suddenly halt launch schedules. Competition in the commercial launch sector from established players like Boeing Co. (BA -1.96%) or Northrop Grumman Corp. (NOC -0.35%) could pressure its pricing power. The company also faces immense technical risks, as launch failures can result in significant financial losses and delays in project timelines.

Lockheed Martin appears much more attractively valued based on its Forward P/E, while Space Exploration Technologies carries a significantly higher multiple due to its growth profile.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

SpaceX's various businesses intend to leverage the tech giant's core launch capabilities, starting with reusable rockets. The ability to reuse boosters significantly lowers per-launch costs and spreads fixed manufacturing costs across multiple missions. Expectations are that scaling up rapidly will happen, with Wall Street analysts projecting $48.9 billion in sales for fiscal 2026, and a swing to profitability, with $4 billion net income projected.

The lack of free cash flow appears to be crushing; projections indicate free cash flow will be negative $59 billion this year, then jump to negative $146 billion in 2027.

Still, the success of Tesla Inc. (TSLA -6.92%) has made founder Elon Musk the richest man in the world and raised expectations that he can make an even greater fortune from SpaceX. The business certainly has market support behind it, raising $85.7 billion this year through what was at the time the world's largest-ever IPO.

SpaceX has a very real business in Starlink, which mitigates the possibility that grander intends won't come to fruition. But the company doesn't have a monopoly on any of its businesses--there are other space cargo and reusable rocket competitors, other space-based Internet and mobile phone networks, and plenty of AI competitors.

In a recent development, lockheed Martin Corp. is a core tech giant in U.S. aerospace and defense. In particular, the F-35 fighter program remains a pillar of Lockheed's business, with the Defense Department planning to continue to buy the jet into the 2040s. Having more than a quarter of revenue essentially guaranteed for 15 years or more is unheard of and quite appealing to a long-term investor. In addition to jet fighters, the company has a handful of drone systems it claims can integrate into U.S. defense systems to provide a blanket of security systems to complement the jets.

Lockheed's revenue should rise 8% this year to $81 billion, with a much healthier 40% jump in net income to more than $7 billion.

SpaceX has the buzz, but shares come at a sky-high premium. Lockheed Martin's equity is priced at a discount to the S&P 500's average P/E and P/S ratios. That's a good deal for a tech giant that has predictable revenue for the foreseeable future given its role in American defense. Long-term investors should go with Lockheed Martin shares.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Oura developed a tool for its frequent-flying members that could help them stave off the worst of jet lag.

Ahead of the busy holiday travel season, on Tuesday, Oura declared Jet Lag Plan, a new feature designed to help travelers feel alert and energized after crossing several time zones.

Also: Oura Ring consumers may get in-app access to real doctors soon – what we know.

Jet Lag Plan takes into account your travel itinerary, sleep patterns, and body responses to provide guidance for traveling members entering new time zones.

Jet lag happens when circadian rhythms are at odds with local time zones, but there are a few things people can do to adjust.

Oura factors in the direction of travel, how many time zones are crossed, individual light windows, and sleep timing.

Ring consumers will enter their flight details, including information like multi-stop trips, and also include the reason for the trip. Oura adjusts the Jet Lag Plan accordingly, and a business trip’s plan may differ in intensity from that of a vacation.

“Two people on the same flight can get different looks, because guidance reflects your itinerary, your typical sleep schedule, and your chronotype,” Oura writes in a blog post. The chronotype refers to Oura’s sleep chronotype, which categorizes people into six types (early morning, morning, early evening, and so on) based on their historical sleep activity.

Also: I wore the Oura Ring 5 for a month.

Recent findings suggest that after adding these details, Oura provides each user with timely guidance throughout their trip. This guidance could include recommendations on when to begin or end caffeine consumption or light exposure, and when to start preparing for sleep. The plan is designed for those crossing three or more time zones. Members can follow along with these recommendations by checking them off as they complete each one. Owners can also talk to Oura’s Advisor in the event of flight or timing changes.

Jet Lag Proposal is now available for Oura Members with Oura Ring Gen 3 or later.

Go to your home screen, tap the + and select Jet Lag Blueprint to get started. You can also tell Oura Advisor about a trip to initiate Jet Lag Plan. If the Oura app detects a time zone shift of 3 or more hours, Jet Lag Plan may appear as a push notification.

As StreetInsider.com reports today, memory-market research firm TrendForce just published a negative forecast for NAND flash memory demand in 2027.

Major Chinese cloud providers are likely to cut orders for enterprise SSDs next year, TrendForce warns. Indeed, they're already cutting orders, and NAND spot prices are already down 20% "as distributors clear inventory." This decrease in demand may eliminate pricing pressure on NAND chips, forcing NAND prices lower in Q1 2027, in Q2 2027, and "onward.".

Industry observers note that now, the good news for Micron is that it doesn't just sell NAND. Actually, only about 26% of the organization's revenue comes from NAND, with the balance coming from sales of DRAM. This means that Micron won't be as sensitive to NAND price declines as Sandisk (SNDK -15.76%), for example.

Investors also have to be alert to the risk that the same dynamics that depress demand for NAND may also affect DRAM demand. If we see demand and prices decline there as well, then Micron may fail to dodge this bullet.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In iOS 27, Apple unveiled iPhone Handoff, a networking feature that allows users to switch cell service between two eSIM-enabled iPhones.
  • Code strings include “Use a SIM on two phones,” and note that the feature will be called Fast Switch.
  • Also: Why your USB-C cables look alike, but work differently – and how to tell them apart.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In iOS 27, Apple unveiled iPhone Handoff, a networking feature that allows users to switch cell service between two eSIM-enabled iPhones. Text strings in Google’s SIM Manager app suggest the tech giant is preparing a similar feature for compatible Android phones, according to Android Authority.

Code strings include “Use a SIM on two phones,” and note that the feature will be called Fast Switch. Little information is currently available about the feature’s limitations, including which phones or mobile carriers may not be compatible.

Also: Why your USB-C cables look alike, but work differently – and how to tell them apart.

On Apple’s side, any iPhone in the US running iOS 27 with a T-Mobile or Verizon-provided eSIM can use iPhone Handoff. AT&T does not at the moment support iPhone Handoff.

However, the code strings uncovered by Android Authority show that Android’s Fast Switch will work similarly to iPhone Handoff, in that customers must be signed in to both devices under the same Google account for the feature to work.

Strings in Google’s SIM Manager app also point to no sharing between two users, so this feature isn’t a way to circumvent carrier fees by adding service to someone else’s phone for the price of one.

According to recent reports, if Fast Switch works anything like iPhone Handoff, which it appears it will, one eSIM can be switched between two phones. So, calls, messages, location services, and other information synced to your Apple ID can remain consistent between two devices.

Also: 5 hidden iOS 27 features that make older iPhones better.

Some third-party apps, like banking, communications, or social media, may also remain consistent across the two phones, depending on the app’s syncing behavior.

Features like Apple’s iPhone Handoff and Google’s Fast Switch are ideal for people who regularly use two phones. Business owners and digital creators may want one phone strictly for business purposes and the other for personal use.

Also: Google Wallet turns your Android phone into a digital house key.

Recent findings suggest that in that case, one person can keep up with two phones without paying for two phone service lines through their carrier. Still, users will incur a fee, as T-Mobile charges $5/month for iPhone Handoff, while Verizon charges $10/month.

  • Recent findings suggest that the settings are available now for free and paying users globally, except for those in India, the Philippines and Indonesia.
  • Sources indicate that to turn off Canva’s AI, go to your Profile > Settings > Preferences and toggle Enable generative AI features on or off.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it’s a great day for designers who hate AI. Canva, the online design and publishing platform, revealed on Thursday that it’s introducing two latest settings to opt out of seeing and using AI tools. One lets you turn off AI tools in Canva, and the other lets you filter out AI-created content from Canva’s library of templates and other elements.

Recent findings suggest that the settings are available now for free and paying users globally, except for those in India, the Philippines and Indonesia. Canva administrators for business and team plans can enable the two fresh settings for their entire organization.

Sources indicate that to turn off Canva’s AI, go to your Profile > Settings > Preferences and toggle Enable generative AI features on or off. To filter out AI in your Canva library, go to Profile > Your account > AI personalization and enable the feature that indicates show less AI-generated content.

It’s hard not to compare Canva’s new opt-out features to Adobe, which spent all of last week at Adobe Max trying to convince creative professionals to embrace its AI tools. Adobe’s chief technology officer told CNET that he thought the problem was slop, not AI.

As criticisms of AI mount, it’s smart, albeit rare, to see a tech company give its people a definitive, one-click solution to filter out AI tools. We will have to put Canva’s settings to the test to see how effectively they work, though.

Industry observers note that if you do want to use AI, Canva has no shortage. Its magic layers tool lets you break apart an AI-generated image into editable layers, a hugely helpful capability for fixing errors and customizing content. Its foundational models, along with other third-party models, can help you generate new image, video and audio content. Outside of graphic design, Canva has added AI tools for spreadsheet, document and presentation work over the past year. And like every other tech company, Canva notes it intends to continue investing in AI.

For more, check out our guides to muting Meta AI and disabling Google’s AI on your Pixel.

  • Also: 5 apps I need Siri AI to work with now that it’s open to third-party developers.
  • Sources indicate that apple hasn’t been shy about stating that the use of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence for specific tasks would face daily access limits.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Have you been using the upcoming Siri AI? If so, how much? I’ve been turning to it a lot since the release of iOS 27. Well, how we use it — and how often — will soon depend on how much we pay for an iCloud+ plan.

Also: 5 apps I need Siri AI to work with now that it’s open to third-party developers.

Sources indicate that apple hasn’t been shy about stating that the use of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence for specific tasks would face daily access limits. Increased limits would be granted based on your iCloud+ subscription. Now the firm has revealed how much it will cost you and when the limits will begin.

Recent findings suggest that “Starting with the 2027 software releases, Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features are available for free for users with a supported device set to a supported language,” Apple said on a support page updated November 16. “Some features rely on powerful server models and have limits where increased access is available with eligible iCloud+ plans, starting with the 27.3 release.”.

iOS 27.3 is expected to launch in early December, so that’s when the daily usage limits will kick in.

At that point, people with no paid iCloud+ plan and even those with the $0.99-per-month 50 GB plan will be the most limited, with Apple saying only that they’ll face a “Standard Device Limit.”.

What is a standard limit? That depends not just on how many times you tap into Siri per day but on what tasks you assign it. Basic Siri commands, such as setting timers and alarms or sending standard text messages, will remain free and unlimited.

In a recent development, also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.

Advanced Siri and Apple Intelligence tasks will bump into the usage limits. These include the following, according to Apple:.

One positive here is that the limits are per device not per account. That means you can use Siri AI and Apple Intelligence with the same account across your iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, and Vision Pro without fear of chewing up too much of your quota.

Sources indicate that this all sounds like a way for Apple to steer people to more expensive iCloud+ accounts. But the limits are in place for a key reason. Basic commands are processed on your device, so they don’t require the use of Apple servers. More advanced tasks are processed using server-side AI models, which can feel the strain if too many people access them all at once.

Also: What you’ll pay for AI agents will be wildly variable and unpredictable.

Industry observers note that how will you know if you use up your daily allotment and what happens then? You’ll receive a notification if you hit your limit for a particular feature category. At that point, you can still give Siri basic tasks to perform. But advanced ones will be paused until your limit resets the next day. Otherwise, Apple is undoubtedly hoping that people who continually run into limits will upgrade to a pricier iCloud+ plan.

#16323. Breaking: iPhone Duo, One Month Later: I’m Not Ready to End the Love Affair

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1976 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: iPhone Duo, One Month Later: I’m Not Ready to End the Love Affair

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1976 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • One month after getting the iPhone Duo, I’ve stuck to my commitment to keep using it even after publishing my review.
  • According to recent reports, apple’s debut foldable has proven to be a practical everyday device, whether I’m streaming movies, texting or getting work done.
  • It has been revealed that still, there have been times when I’ve reached for the iPhone 18 Pro Max instead for its more advanced camera system, as well as its familiar, straightforward design.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One month after getting the iPhone Duo, I’ve stuck to my commitment to keep using it even after publishing my review. Well, mostly.

According to recent reports, apple’s debut foldable has proven to be a practical everyday device, whether I’m streaming movies, texting or getting work done. I’ve grown so accustomed to using it that I sometimes forget how much attention it draws when I pull it out of my pocket, especially given its limited availability and lengthy preorder windows – not to mention its sky-high $1,999 starting price.

It has been revealed that still, there have been times when I’ve reached for the iPhone 18 Pro Max instead for its more advanced camera system, as well as its familiar, straightforward design. The Duo’s cameras pull their weight with casual photography, but while filming social content at F1’s US Grand Prix and chatting with filmmakers at an SFFilm screening, I couldn’t resist going for the best cameras at my disposal on the Pro Max. There are times a conventional slab phone just does the trick – without all the frills and novelty of a folding one.

It has been revealed that that hasn’t stopped me from keeping the Duo as my primary device. It’s an enjoyable phone to use, with its compact, palm-sized build and spacious inner display. Plus, as CNET’s ongoing folding test demonstrates, it has a durable build that ensures I can fold and unfold it to my heart’s content.

And if I’m being honest, I kind of love how much of a statement piece it’s become.

Recent findings suggest that the Duo’s versatility has really shown its appeal the more I live with it. I find myself using the 5.4-inch cover screen and 7.6-inch inner display pretty equally, demonstrating the practicality of each.

It has been revealed that when I’m on the move, the cover screen suffices for sending texts, responding to emails and checking notifications. Lounging around at home, I’m more inclined to use the larger inner display to endlessly scroll through Instagram or binge YouTube videos.

Recent findings suggest that the matte inner display remains one of my favorite elements. It reduces the appearance of the crease as well as glare, making it easier to see content even outdoors. Yes, the coating can dim the vibrant colors in images and videos, even with the screen’s 3,000-nit peak brightness, and smudges become prominent. But I can live with both of those drawbacks, and a microfiber cloth fixes the latter.

Sources indicate that apple’s phone-tablet hybrid came in clutch when I was on a recent flight and didn’t want to pull out my laptop. Instead, I used the Duo’s split-screen mode to place the Notes app on one half of the screen and an informational video on the other so I could quickly jot down the main points. The Duo has also become my gym buddy; I prop it open on the treadmill so I can watch Magpie Murders on a tablet-like display, then fold it up and toss it in my pocket when I’m done.

Apple Pencil support really helps the Duo feel like a mini iPad, and the matte coating on the inner display adds a satisfying resistance that more closely emulates the feel of writing on paper than a glossy surface. It gives jotting down notes, highlighting book passages and marking up documents a more tactile feel. I’m not much of a doodler, but I imagine that’s fun, too.

In a recent development, the Apple Pencil can magnetically attach to the outer surface of the hinge, though it definitely sticks out, so there’s not really a practical, secure way to carry it around with the Duo (at least not that Apple has shared, but case-makers are sure to cook up a solution). I’m glad the stylus also works on the Duo’s cover screen, though the smaller size and glossy display make that experience slightly less satisfying.

It has been revealed that the number of apps optimized for the Duo at launch was relatively small, but it’s steadily increased. I gasped aloud on the train platform one morning while sending an email, realizing Gmail had finally been adapted for the Duo. It’s refreshing to see apps that feel intentional and fill the screen, rather than being awkwardly letterboxed.

Apple said in early November that more than 100,000 apps built for the iPhone Duo were live in the App Store. A week later, that number ballooned to over 200,000 apps. So despite a rather slow start, virtually all apps I regularly use now work seamlessly on Apple’s foldable.

In a recent development, one of my favorite apps on the Duo is Instagram’s Edits. When holding the phone open in landscape orientation, I can view the video timeline and make edits on the right side of the screen while seeing a preview of the video on the left. Rotated to portrait orientation, the layout resembles the interface on a traditional smartphone, but on a larger scale, which is helpful especially for making smaller tweaks.

It’s great to see more apps that don’t just expand to the larger screen, but make meaningful use of the Duo’s design.

As I found during my review, the Duo’s battery life has been pretty good. It consistently lasts through the day, even as I hop between displays. I usually charge my phone at night, but even if I don’t, I know I’ll have some remaining battery in the morning.

In a recent development, for instance, one day I started at 6:30 a.m. with a full battery. After my usual routine of checking emails, texting, scrolling through social media and browsing YouTube throughout the day, my battery was at 55% by 9:12 p.m. The next morning, I woke up with 48% battery, and that charge lasted through a similar routine, along with phone calls, texting and music and video streaming, before the battery finally died at 7:30 p.m.

The Duo has yet to give me a reason to stress about its battery life.

In a recent development, I will acknowledge I’m a tad pretentious when it comes to smartphone cameras. But if I’m documenting an event or photographing my fancy tea sets, I want the best cameras I can get. Unlike the Duo, iPhone 18 Pro models have a telephoto camera, more advanced optical zoom capabilities and larger main-camera sensors.

Most of the time, the Duo’s 48-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras do the trick just fine. Colors are vivid, details are sharp and images are bright. Videos look good, too, though the 18 Pro Max does a noticeably better job with nighttime footage, which can look more muddy on the Duo. Digital video on the Duo also tops out at 6x, versus 24x on the Pros. Most of the time, though, I’m quite content with what I capture with the Duo’s cameras.

Industry observers note that as I noted in my review, the under-display FaceTime camera on the inner screen isn’t great, but I never really take selfies using that camera. It feels much more natural to use the 12-megapixel selfie camera on the cover screen, which serves up sharp photos every time.

The cover screen selfie camera plays a critical role in an update that makes using the Duo even more seamless. In its latest iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple added an option to unlock the iPhone Duo using the front camera.

In a recent development, in the absence of Face ID, which I have felt rather painfully, this has been a solid workaround, even if it’s not as secure as Apple’s biometric facial recognition and authentication system. You’ll still need to use Touch ID or a passcode when using Apple Pay or accessing passwords, and to unlock the phone after leaving it alone for around 45 minutes. But a win is a win. (You can also unlock the Duo using an Apple Watch, but I don’t have one.).

I’ll admit I still feel a little bashful when pulling out the Duo because of how much attention it drums up, despite being far from the first foldable phone. But its limited availability and hype paired with the unique design make it eye-catching, for better or worse. Using the Duo has led to some fun conversations, whether it’s with a sales associate as I pay for a pastry or with Project Hail Mary directors Phil Lord and Chris Miller, who spotted the phone in my hand during an interview and geeked out over it. That’s been a fun side effect of using Apple’s first foldable in my everyday life.

Sources indicate that I’ve been living dangerously without a case; I don’t want anything to detract from the phone’s sleek feel. This is one of those “do as I say, not as I do” moments, as I’d recommend slapping a case on a phone that costs nearly $2,000. I did put a tempered glass screen protector on the cover display to guard against scratches. I can feel its edge against the otherwise flush surface of the phone when I hold it open, but aesthetic sacrifices must be made.

The Duo isn’t perfect, even if I love using this phone. After holding Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8, the iPhone Duo can feel slightly chunky. The Z Fold 8 measures 4.5mm thick when open and 9.7mm when closed. Meanwhile, the Duo is 5.2mm thick when open and 11.3mm when closed. It’s not a huge difference, but it makes me look forward to Apple hopefully slimming down the second-generation version, if and when it comes.

The Duo is also slightly heavier than the Z Fold 8, weighing 254 grams (compared to 201 grams for Samsung’s foldable). I’m always surprised when people remark how heavy the Duo is, but I think the reason I don’t share that sentiment is that I’m accustomed to the iPhone 18 Pro Max, which weighs 249 grams.

In a recent development, when the Duo is open in landscape orientation, I’m glad there’s an option to split the keyboard so it’s easier to type across the wider expanse, but I wish the swipe functionality worked in that configuration, too. It’s a little thing that would make a noticeable difference for those of us who rely heavily on swipe-to-text.

One drawback of the Duo’s compact design is that some existing MagSafe wallets and other accessories won’t stick to the back without awkwardly jutting out. So you might have to invest in some new accessories specifically designed for the Duo.

Until the recent addition of face unlock, the Duo’s biggest drawback was the lack of Face ID. It’s a feature I’d expect on such a premium device, especially given that even the budget-focused iPhone 17E supports it.

Recent findings suggest that touch ID works reliably on the Duo, but it’s slow compared to fingerprint unlock on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 (which also supports facial recognition). And while the latest face unlock capability on the Duo isn’t an exact replacement for Face ID, which is more secure, it helps make accessing the phone’s contents more convenient and in line with the Duo’s modern aesthetics.

Recent findings suggest that I’ve finished my homework: My review is done, and now, so is this one-month follow-up. What’s next?

I’m not sure I’m ready to throw in the towel on Apple’s foldable just yet. The novelty of the iPhone Duo hasn’t worn off, and I’ve become quite used to my passport-size companion. It does just about everything I need, despite some slight imperfections, and it’s fun to use. It’s also amusing to see how people react when they see it in my hand.

According to recent reports, so for now, it looks like the Duo will remain my daily driver. Whether the honeymoon phase eventually wears off remains to be seen, but I’m not in any hurry to end this love affair.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google’s Gemini can now turn your notes and other sources in your Gemini Notebook (previously called NotebookLM) into interactive pages or sites to help you better process complicated information.
  • Sources indicate that complete with flashcards, dashboards, and colorful panels, the sites make it easier to study and understand intricate concepts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google’s Gemini can now turn your notes and other sources in your Gemini Notebook (previously called NotebookLM) into interactive pages or sites to help you better process complicated information.

Sources indicate that complete with flashcards, dashboards, and colorful panels, the sites make it easier to study and understand intricate concepts. I tested the feature, unveiled Tuesday, to see how efficient it is at creating a navigable site that is actually helpful and stays loyal to sources.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s newly introduced Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector in my tests.

Because Notebooks are built with the sources you provide, like textbooks, files, or notes, the sites are created with the data that is in your Gemini Notebook. Notebook has three tabs: Sources, Chat, and Studio. The site option is in the Studio tab, listed under what you can create.

If you’re taking a college class, you could put all the information you need to prepare for a test and use the interactive site as a study guide that you can share with others.

To test this, I gave Notebook the following prompt:.

“Make me a site that visually explains how cellular respiration works, breaking down each stage with interactive diagrams and self-check flashcards.”.

Since I’m not in a class that would give me those study materials, I gave Gemini online sources to use for this.   • Recent findings suggest that if you only looked at Pasqal Holding (PSQL +5.83%) stock's chart, you'd assume something broke.
  • It has been revealed that but when I dug into what the manufacturer has actually been doing, I didn't find a broken business.
  • There are numerous ways to create the quantum bits — aka, qubits — that sit at the heart of every quantum computer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Micah Zimmerman – Nov 20, 2026 at 11:47AM EST.

Recent findings suggest that if you only looked at Pasqal Holding (PSQL +5.83%) stock's chart, you'd assume something broke. The French quantum computer maker hit $24.69 a share within days of its Nasdaq debut in late August. Today, it trades at around $3.

It has been revealed that but when I dug into what the manufacturer has actually been doing, I didn't find a broken business. I found one that's ahead of its stock. That gap is why I think Pasqal could be the biggest winner in quantum computing next year.

NASDAQ · As of 2:14 PM ET 11/20/26.

There are numerous ways to create the quantum bits — aka, qubits — that sit at the heart of every quantum computer.

According to recent reports, pasqal is taking the “neutral-atom qubit” approach, creating each qubit from a single rubidium atom held in place and manipulated by lasers. One advantage of this method is that its machines don't need powerful cryogenic cooling systems to bring them to temperatures near absolute zero, which some more commonly pursued qubit technologies require.

In a recent development, that makes it easier to install them in the same rooms as ordinary server racks, and Pasqal has seven of them deployed across three continents, plus factories in France and Canada built to turn out up to 13 machines a year. CEO Wasiq Bokhari indicates that its hardware design will scale to at least 10,000 qubits per machine by 2029.

"Customers don't care whether it's a quantum computer or a GPU," he told analysts in June. "They just want the problem solved.".

The best example among its current customers is energy megacap Saudi Aramco, which formally launched a 200-qubit Pasqal machine at its data center in May and now offers cloud access to it for other companies.

In a recent development, "Aramco is not just waiting for quantum computing, it is helping to shape it," Bokhari mentioned. Pasqal has also signed a partnership with LG's tech arm in South Korea and a joint venture agreement to deploy systems across Saudi Arabia. It even launched a plug-in that lets AI coding assistants turn a research idea into a running experiment on its cloud machines.

The big catalyst due to arrive in 2027 is Vela, the next machine on Pasqal's roadmap, which will have 200-plus qubits. CTO Loïc Henriet described Vela as the machine that will "bring the first quantum advantage use cases to our clients." In plain English, that means it should be able to solve real business problems faster than a traditional GPU-powered server cluster can. Pasqal also aims to have systems providing 20 error-corrected "logical" qubits in production by 2027.

Sources indicate that the science is already getting interesting. In October, its 256-qubit processor revealed magnet behavior that theory didn't predict. "We are not simply reproducing what we already know, but uncovering behavior we did not expect," Henriet remarked.

In a recent development, the catch is that roadmaps slip. Vela is a target, not a product on a shelf, and if it arrives late or underwhelms, the 2027 story will fall apart.

The business’s financial numbers are small and bumpy. In the third quarter, revenue fell to 3.3 million euros, from 5.7 million euros a year earlier, because Pasqal sold no machines during the quarter. Revenue from services like cloud access, upgrades, and maintenance did jump 53%, but that wasn't enough to compensate for the lack of new quantum computer orders. However, Bokhari said: "Although the order book and revenue do not show it yet, we have made important progress in our technology roadmap.".

Recent findings suggest that in September, Pasqal also exited a French defense quantum program to focus on commercial work. The cash story is mixed, too. In June, CFO Stéphane Rougeot remarked the SPAC merger that it was using to join the public market could leave Pasqal with "north of $600 million." In August, the actual deal netted it about $360 million. During its analyst day presentation in June, Rougeot also mentioned that the firm had secured a $250 million convertible note, which could turn into new shares and dilute today's owners.

Here's why I still like the setup. Pasqal ended September with 312.8 million euros in cash and equivalents on its balance sheet, and its market cap is only about $681 million. Rougeot noted annual cash burn has been between 30 million euros and 50 million euros, should rise only modestly, and that "we have plenty of runway." At this price, investors are paying very little for the technology itself.

In a recent development, that's what makes a "biggest winner" call possible. A stock already priced for disappointment doesn't need perfection to soar. Pasqal just needs Vela to show up and work. If it delivers its first system providing a quantum advantage to customers in 2027, I expect the market will stop pricing it as a failed experiment.
